机器人软件 · 从总线到 ROS · 从下往上Robot software · From buses to ROS · From the bottom up

一台机器人，几十个程序One Robot, Dozens of Programs

厨房机器人的团队这回要让机器人真的动起来。它有一条七个关节的手臂，每 1 毫秒要和控制电脑交换一次数据，晚了这一拍的指令就被扔掉；头上一个深度相机，每秒送来 30 帧彩色图和 30 帧深度图，一秒一百多 MB；底盘前面一个激光雷达，每秒扫 40 圈；两个轮子的电机挂在一条每秒只能传一百万个比特的总线上，由一块单片机管着；车里还有一块 Jetson Thor、一台专跑实时内核的小电脑，再通过 Wi-Fi 连着团队的工作站。装在上面的程序有几十个：相机驱动、雷达驱动、手臂控制器、目标检测、模仿学习的策略、运动规划、导航、录数据的、给人看的……它们由不同的人、用不同的语言写成，跑在不同的机器上，频率从每秒 1000 次到每秒 10 次。大家说，把它们管起来的办法就是 ROS。可 ROS 到底是什么？它是一个操作系统吗？没有它的时候大家怎么办？它为什么老是升级就坏，为什么用它的人都写 C++？这一篇从最底下讲起：先看字节怎样从传感器顺着总线进到内存，再看一台电脑上、几台电脑之间的程序怎样传数据；然后看 ROS 之前的办法、ROS 1、ROS 2，一个节点里面怎样调度，ROS 在 Linux 上的哪一层；再把手臂的 1 毫秒回路、MoveIt 的规划、坐标变换和导航拆开；最后回答版本、语言和别的办法这几个问题，并把这台机器人整个搭一遍。This time the kitchen-robot team is going to make the robot actually move. It has an arm with seven joints that has to exchange data with its control computer once every 1 millisecond, and a command that misses its beat is dropped; a depth camera on its head sends 30 colour frames and 30 depth frames every second, more than 100 MB a second; a lidar at the front of the base scans 40 times a second; the two wheel motors sit on a bus that can carry only one million bits a second, with a microcontroller in charge of them; on board there are also a Jetson Thor and a small computer set aside to run a real-time kernel, and the robot is linked over Wi-Fi to the team’s workstation. Several dozen programs are installed on it: the camera driver, the lidar driver, the arm controller, object detection, an imitation-learning policy, motion planning, navigation, programs that record data, programs for people to look at … They are written by different people in different languages and run on different machines, at rates from 1000 times a second down to 10 times a second. Everyone says the way to manage them all is ROS. But what is ROS, really? Is it an operating system? What did people do before it existed? Why does it break every time you upgrade, and why does everyone who uses it write C++? This page starts from the very bottom: first how bytes travel from a sensor along a bus into memory, then how programs pass data on one computer and between several computers; next, how people did things before ROS, then ROS 1 and ROS 2, how scheduling works inside one node, and which layer of a Linux system ROS sits in; after that it takes apart the arm’s 1-millisecond loop, MoveIt’s planning, coordinate transforms and navigation; and finally it answers the questions about versions, languages and the other ways, and puts the whole robot together from start to finish.

读法先把公式念成一句话Read it asFirst say the formula as a sentence
为什么为什么偏偏是这个样子Why this wayWhy it has to look like this
符号每个字母、记号是什么意思SymbolsWhat every letter and sign means
算例代入这台机器人的数验证一遍Worked examplePlug in this robot’s numbers and check
要点最容易出错、最关键的地方Key pointThe part that matters most and is easiest to get wrong
速查忘了某个说法，查下面的速查表LookupForgot a term? Check the table below

单位约定：1 µs（微秒）= 10−6 秒，1 ms（毫秒）= 10−3 秒；1 Hz 是每秒一次，1 kHz 是每秒 1000 次。比特每秒（bit/s）和字节（B）都按 1000 进位：1 Mbit/s = 106 bit/s，1 MB = 106 B；KiB、MiB 按 1024 进位；1 字节 = 8 比特。引用别人的数时照原文的写法。文中说"我们测的"，是在上一篇那台云上的小虚拟机里测的：2 个虚拟 CPU，8 GB 内存，Ubuntu 24.04，Linux 6.18（不是实时内核），Python 3.13；测量用的小程序放在本页仓库的 ros/meas/ 目录里。说"我们数的"，是我们从官方仓库里数出来的（2026 年 11 月的版本）。说"估"的是没有出处的数量级估计，说"示意"的是为了讲清楚而编的例子。Units: 1 µs (microsecond) = 10−6 s, 1 ms (millisecond) = 10−3 s; 1 Hz is once a second and 1 kHz is 1000 times a second. Bits per second (bit/s) and bytes (B) both go up in factors of 1000: 1 Mbit/s = 106 bit/s, 1 MB = 106 B; KiB and MiB go up in factors of 1024; 1 byte = 8 bits. Figures quoted from elsewhere are written as in the source. Where the text says "we measured", the measurement was taken on the small cloud virtual machine from the previous page: 2 virtual CPUs, 8 GB of memory, Ubuntu 24.04, Linux 6.18 (not a real-time kernel), Python 3.13; the small programs we measured with are in the ros/meas/ directory of this page’s repository. Where it says "our count", we counted it ourselves in the official repositories (as of November 2026). Anything marked "est." is an order-of-magnitude estimate with no source, and anything marked "illustrative" is an example made up to make things clear.

速查表：本篇用到的说法、记号和缩写Quick reference: the terms, notation and abbreviations used on this page

硬件和总线Hardware and buses

总线Bus
几台设备共用的一条传数据的线路，比如 USB、以太网、CAN（第 ① 步）a line for carrying data that several devices share, such as USB, Ethernet or CAN (step ①)
带宽Bandwidth
一条线每秒最多能传多少比特（第 ① 步）the most bits a line can carry in a second (step ①)
帧Frame
总线上一次传的一小包数据，前后带着地址、校验这些"包装"（第 ① 步）a small packet of data sent over a bus in one go, with "overhead" such as an address and a checksum at the front and back (step ①)
驱动Driver
让操作系统和程序能用上一个设备的那段代码；有的在内核里，有的是普通程序（第 ① 步）the code that lets the operating system and programs use a device; some drivers are in the kernel, others are ordinary programs (step ①)
单片机Microcontroller
英文 microcontroller（MCU）：一块芯片上的小电脑，没有 Linux，专门跑一个固定的控制程序（第 ①、⑦ 步）MCU for short: a small computer on a single chip; it has no Linux and runs one fixed control program and nothing else (steps ① and ⑦)

一台电脑里Inside one computer

进程、线程Process, thread
一个正在跑的程序，有自己的内存；进程里能同时跑的一条执行路线（第 ② 步，上一篇第 ② 步）a running program, with its own memory; one path of execution inside a process, several of which can run at the same time (step ②; step ② of the previous page)
系统调用System call
程序请内核办事的入口，比如 read、write（第 ② 步）the door through which a program asks the kernel to do something, such as read and write (step ②)
进程间通信Inter-process communication
两个进程交换数据的办法：管道、套接字、共享内存（第 ② 步）the ways two processes exchange data: pipes, sockets, shared memory (step ②)
序列化Serialisation
把内存里的数据结构排成一串字节，好让别的程序读回来（第 ② 步）laying a data structure in memory out as a string of bytes, so that another program can read it back (step ②)
零拷贝Zero copy
数据不复制，直接让对方在原地读（第 ②、⑤、⑥ 步）the data is not copied; the other side reads it right where it is (steps ②, ⑤ and ⑥)

ROS 的说法ROS terms

节点Node
ROS 里的一个参与者，通常就是一个程序（或者程序里的一个对象）（第 ④ 步）a participant in ROS, usually just one program (or one object inside a program) (step ④)
话题、消息Topic, message
一个有名字的数据通道，比如 /scan；在上面流动的一条条数据，类型事先定好（第 ④ 步）a data channel with a name, such as /scan; the individual pieces of data flowing along it, whose type is fixed in advance (step ④)
服务、动作Service, action
一问一答的调用；能持续汇报进度、能中途取消的长任务（第 ④、⑦ 步）a call with one request and one reply; a long task that reports its progress as it goes and can be cancelled part-way through (steps ④ and ⑦)
参数Parameter
节点的配置项，比如一个控制器的增益（第 ④ 步）one of a node’s settings, such as a controller’s gain (step ④)
主节点Master
ROS 1 里记着"谁发布什么、谁订阅什么"的那个程序，像一本电话簿（第 ④ 步）the program in ROS 1 that keeps track of "who publishes what and who subscribes to what", like a phone book (step ④)
发现Discovery
节点们不靠电话簿，自己互相找到对方的过程（第 ⑤ 步）the process by which nodes find one another on their own, without a phone book (step ⑤)
中间件、DDSMiddleware, DDS
在程序之间传消息的那层软件；DDS 是工业界的一个中间件标准（第 ⑤ 步）the layer of software that carries messages between programs; DDS is an industry standard for middleware (step ⑤)
QoS
服务质量：一个话题要不要保证送到、新来的订阅者要不要补发旧消息等等（第 ⑤ 步）quality of service: whether a topic’s messages must be guaranteed to arrive, whether old messages are sent again to a subscriber that joins late, and so on (step ⑤)
执行器、回调Executor, callback
一个进程里负责调度回调的那部分（一个执行器可以同时管几个节点）；回调是消息到了、定时到了时被调用的函数（第 ⑥ 步）the part of a process in charge of scheduling the callbacks (one executor can look after several nodes at once); a callback is a function that is called when a message arrives or a timer fires (step ⑥)
坐标系、tfCoordinate frame, tf
一个零件或地方自己的 x、y、z；ROS 里记着各坐标系之间关系的那套库（第 ⑩ 步）a part’s or a place’s own x, y and z; the set of ROS libraries that keeps track of how the frames are related to one another (step ⑩)
发行版Distribution
一套一起发布、一起测试的 ROS 软件包，比如 Humble、Jazzy（第 ⑪ 步）a set of ROS packages that are released and tested together, such as Humble or Jazzy (step ⑪)

控制和规划Control and planning

实时、截止时间Real-time, deadline
不只要算对，还要按时算完；必须在这个时刻之前完成（第 ⑧ 步）not only getting the computation right but also finishing it on time; the moment by which the work must be done (step ⑧)
迟到、抖动Lateness, jitter
本该醒来的时刻和实际醒来的时刻之差；这个差忽大忽小的程度（第 ⑧ 步）the gap between the moment something should wake up and the moment it actually does; how much that gap jumps about (step ⑧)
控制器管理器、硬件接口Controller manager, hardware interface
ros2_control 里每个周期依次读传感器、算控制、写指令的那个循环；它和真实硬件之间的那层代码（第 ⑧ 步）the loop in ros2_control that, every cycle, reads the sensors, computes the control and writes the commands, in that order; the layer of code between it and the real hardware (step ⑧)
轨迹Trajectory
一串带时间的关节位置，告诉手臂"几秒时到哪"（第 ⑨ 步）a series of joint positions, each with a time, that tells the arm "where to be at what second" (step ⑨)
规划场景、碰撞检测Planning scene, collision checking
规划器眼里的世界：机器人和障碍物；判断一个姿态会不会撞上东西（第 ⑨ 步）the world as the planner sees it: the robot and the obstacles; working out whether a pose would hit anything (step ⑨)
代价地图、行为树Costmap, behaviour tree
导航用的一张"哪里不好走"的格子图；把一个任务拆成一棵节点树来执行的办法（第 ⑩ 步）a grid map of "where it is hard to go", used for navigation; a way of carrying out a task by breaking it into a tree of nodes (step ⑩)

记号Notation

L, B, p, h
一条消息的字节数；总线的带宽；一帧能装的字节数；每帧的包装（第 ① 步）the number of bytes in a message; the bandwidth of the bus; how many bytes one frame can hold; the overhead on each frame (step ①)
c0, k, β
传一条消息的固定开销；数据被复制的次数；复制的速度（第 ② 步）the fixed cost of passing one message; the number of times the data is copied; how fast it is copied (step ②)
N
要连在一起的程序个数（第 ③ 步）the number of programs that have to be connected together (step ③)
Ci, Ti, U
一个回调跑一次要多久；它的周期；所有回调加起来占用 CPU 的比例（第 ⑥ 步）how long one run of a callback takes; its period; the fraction of the CPU that all the callbacks take up together (step ⑥)
d, v, a
关节要转过的角度；最大角速度；最大角加速度（第 ⑨ 步）the angle a joint has to turn through; the maximum angular velocity; the maximum angular acceleration (step ⑨)
TAB
把坐标系 B 里的点换到坐标系 A 里的变换（第 ⑩ 步）the transform that takes a point in frame B into frame A (step ⑩)
P, p, k
项目用到的包在新发行版里全都有的概率；一个包也有的概率；项目用到的包数（第 ⑪ 步；和第 ①、② 步的 p、k 不是一回事）the probability that the new distribution has every package the project uses; the probability that it has any one of them; the number of packages the project uses (step ⑪; not the same p and k as in steps ① and ②)
f, c, s
每秒处理几次；处理一次要多久；占一个 CPU 核的比例（第 ⑫ 步；这里的 c 和第 ② 步的 c 不是一回事）how many times a second something is processed; how long processing it once takes; the share of one CPU core this takes up (step ⑫; this c is not the same as the c of step ②)

缩写Abbreviations

ROS
Robot Operating System，名字里有"操作系统"，其实不是（第 ⑦ 步）Robot Operating System: the name says "operating system", but it is not one (step ⑦)
FCI
Franka Control Interface，Franka 手臂对外的 1 kHz 控制接口（第 0、⑧ 步）Franka Control Interface, the Franka arm’s external 1 kHz control interface (steps 0 and ⑧)
IMU
惯性测量单元：测加速度和角速度的小芯片inertial measurement unit: a small chip that measures acceleration and angular velocity
LTS
长期支持版：Ubuntu 每两年一个，ROS 2 跟着它（第 ⑪ 步）long-term support release: Ubuntu brings one out every two years, and ROS 2 keeps in step with it (step ⑪)
RT
real-time，实时（第 ⑧ 步）real-time (step ⑧)

第 0 步 · 一台机器人Step 0 · One robot

一台机器人，几十个程序One Robot, Dozens of Programs

先把这台机器人说清楚。它是虚构的，可每个零件都是真的产品，参数照着厂家的说明书来：First, let’s be clear about this robot. It is fictional, but every part is a real product, with the specifications taken from the manufacturers’ documentation:

  • 手臂：Franka Research 3，七个关节，每个关节里都有力矩传感器，末端是 Franka 自己的夹爪。外面的电脑通过它的控制接口 FCI 指挥它：每 1 毫秒交换一次数据，控制电脑必须跑 PREEMPT_RT 实时内核（Franka 的文档写的是"打了 PREEMPT_RT 补丁的内核"，从 Linux 6.12 起它已经并进主线，第 ⑧ 步）；"网络往返 + 你自己的控制代码 + 机器人那边的处理"加起来必须少于 1 毫秒，否则这一次的指令就被扔掉，连着扔 20 次，机器人就停下来报错（Franka 文档）。Arm: Franka Research 3, with seven joints, a torque sensor in every joint and Franka’s own gripper at the end. An outside computer commands it through its control interface, FCI: they exchange data every 1 ms, and the control computer must run a PREEMPT_RT real-time kernel (Franka’s documentation says "PREEMPT_RT patched kernel"; since Linux 6.12 it has been part of the mainline kernel, step ⑧); "network round trip + your own control code + the processing on the robot’s side" must add up to less than 1 ms, otherwise that command is dropped, and after 20 drops in a row the robot stops with an error (Franka docs).
  • 头部相机：RealSense D435i（原来是 Intel 的产品，2025 年 RealSense 从 Intel 独立出来，公告），经 USB 3.1 Gen 1 接到 Thor 上；深度图最大 1280 × 720（这个分辨率最高每秒 30 帧，要每秒 90 帧得降到 848 × 480 或更低），彩色图最大 1920 × 1080、每秒 30 帧，里面还有一个 IMU（产品页）。团队用的是彩色和深度都 1280 × 720、每秒 30 帧。Head camera: RealSense D435i (originally an Intel product; in 2025 RealSense became independent of Intel, announcement), connected to the Thor over USB 3.1 Gen 1; depth images go up to 1280 × 720 (at that resolution, 30 frames per second at most; for 90 frames per second you have to drop to 848 × 480 or lower), colour images up to 1920 × 1080 at 30 frames per second, and there is an IMU inside as well (product page). The team uses 1280 × 720 at 30 frames per second for both colour and depth.
  • 激光雷达：Hokuyo UST-10LX，装在底盘前面，每 25 毫秒扫一圈（每秒 40 圈），扫 270°，每 0.25° 一个点，一圈 1081 个点，用百兆网线（100BASE-TX）接到 Thor（Hokuyo）。Lidar: Hokuyo UST-10LX, mounted at the front of the base; it completes one scan every 25 ms (40 scans per second), covering 270° with one point every 0.25°, 1081 points per scan, and connects to the Thor with a 100-megabit Ethernet cable, 100BASE-TX (Hokuyo).
  • 底盘：两个轮子，电机驱动器挂在一条经典 CAN 总线上（每秒最多 1 兆比特），由一块单片机管着；单片机通过 USB 串口和 Thor 说话（示意）。Base: two wheels, whose motor drivers sit on a classic CAN bus (at most 1 Mbit/s), managed by a microcontroller; the microcontroller talks to the Thor over USB serial (illustrative).
  • 计算：一块 Jetson AGX Thor（上一篇的 G，现在跑 JetPack 7.2.1，也就是 Ubuntu 24.04），跑相机和雷达的驱动、目标检测、学出来的策略、运动规划和导航；一台装实时内核的小 x86 电脑，专门跑手臂那 1 毫秒一圈的控制（上一篇 E 的答案：单独的实时控制器）；那块单片机；还有通过 Wi-Fi 连着的团队工作站，用来看画面、调试和训练。Compute: a Jetson AGX Thor (the previous page’s request G, now running JetPack 7.2.1, that is, Ubuntu 24.04), which runs the camera and lidar drivers, object detection, the learned policy, motion planning and navigation; a small x86 computer with a real-time kernel that runs nothing but the arm’s control loop, one cycle every 1 ms (the answer to the previous page’s request E: a separate real-time controller); that microcontroller; and the team’s workstation, connected over Wi-Fi, for watching the images, debugging and training.

这台机器人一秒钟里要流过多少东西？手臂那边，每秒 1000 个状态包送上来、1000 个指令包送下去；相机每秒 30 帧彩色图（一帧 1280 × 720 × 3 = 2,764,800 字节）和 30 帧深度图（一帧 1280 × 720 × 2 = 1,843,200 字节），合起来每秒约 138.2 MB（这是发成 ROS 消息以后的大小：彩色图在 USB 线上走的是相机自己的 YUYV 格式，每像素 2 字节，到了 Thor 上才转成 RGB，所以 USB 线上约 110.6 MB/s）；雷达每秒 40 圈，一圈存成 ROS 的激光消息（每个点一个距离、一个强度，各 4 字节）约 8.65 kB；再加上底盘的里程计、导航每秒 20 次发给底盘的速度指令（Nav2 的默认值）、策略每秒约 10 次的动作（估）……装在上面的程序，一数就有二三十个。它们由不同的人、用 C++ 或 Python 写成，跑在三四台不同的机器上，频率差了 100 倍，消息大小差了十万倍。要让它们一起干活，得先解决一串很实际的问题：How much has to flow through this robot in one second? On the arm’s side, every second 1000 state packets come up and 1000 command packets go down; the camera sends 30 colour frames a second (1280 × 720 × 3 = 2,764,800 bytes each) and 30 depth frames (1280 × 720 × 2 = 1,843,200 bytes each), about 138.2 MB/s together (that is the size once they are published as ROS messages: on the USB cable the colour image travels in the camera’s own YUYV format, 2 bytes per pixel, and is converted to RGB only on the Thor, so the USB cable carries about 110.6 MB/s); the lidar does 40 scans a second, and one scan, stored as a ROS laser message (one range and one intensity per point, 4 bytes each), is about 8.65 kB; on top of that come the base’s odometry, the velocity commands that navigation sends to the base 20 times a second (Nav2’s default), the policy’s actions, about 10 a second (est.) … Count the programs installed on it and there are twenty or thirty. They are written by different people in C++ or Python and run on three or four different machines; their rates differ by a factor of 100, and their message sizes by a factor of 100,000. To make them work together, you first have to solve a string of very practical problems:

  • 找到对方：检测程序怎么知道相机图从哪来？换了一台电脑跑，地址变了怎么办？Finding each other: how does the detection program know where the camera images come from? And if it moves to another computer and the address changes, what then?
  • 说同一种话：一帧图里先放宽还是先放高？时间戳用什么单位？改了一个字段，旧程序还认不认？Speaking the same language: in an image, does the width come first or the height? What unit are the time stamps in? If you change one field, will the old programs still accept it?
  • 按时：手臂的 1 毫秒一拍，怎么不被检测程序的 30 毫秒拖住？Keeping time: how do you stop the arm’s 1 ms beat from being held up by the detection program’s 30 ms?
  • 管起来：二三十个程序按什么顺序启动？参数放哪？一个崩了怎么办？Managing them: in what order should twenty or thirty programs start? Where do the parameters go? What if one of them crashes?
  • 看得见、录得下：调试时想看相机图、坐标系、规划出来的轨迹；想把一次失败录下来，回到办公室再放一遍。Seeing and recording: while debugging, you want to see the camera images, the coordinate frames and the planned trajectories; you want to record a failure and play it back again at the office.
  • 换得动：换一个相机、换一条手臂、换一种规划算法，要改多少地方？Swapping parts: swap the camera, the arm or the planning algorithm, and how many places do you have to change?

大多数机器人团队的回答是 ROS。可它到底在哪一层回答这些问题、回答得怎么样，要一层层往下看。这一篇要回答八个问题：Most robotics teams answer: ROS. But to see at which layer it really answers these questions, and how well, we have to go through the layers one at a time. This page sets out to answer eight questions:

  1. 控制一台机器人到底要管住哪些东西，为什么需要一套统一的系统？What exactly do you have to keep in hand to control a robot, and why do you need one unified system for it?
  2. ROS 出现以前，大家怎么做？问题在哪？Before ROS came along, how did people do it? What was the problem?
  3. ROS 到底是什么？它是不是一个操作系统，和 Linux 是什么关系？What is ROS, really? Is it an operating system, and what is its relationship with Linux?
  4. ROS 能做什么、不能做什么？MoveIt、Nav2、ros2_control 这些组件各在哪一层？What can ROS do, and what can’t it do? At which layer does each of these components, MoveIt, Nav2 and ros2_control, sit?
  5. 为什么 ROS 的版本兼容这么麻烦，这和它"让代码能复用"的愿景冲突吗？Why is version compatibility in ROS such a headache, and does that contradict its vision of "making code reusable"?
  6. 为什么用 ROS 的人大多写 C++，Python 用得少？Why do most people who use ROS write C++, and comparatively few use Python?
  7. ROS 是唯一的选择吗？别的办法各为什么诞生，各有什么优劣？Is ROS the only choice? Why was each of the other approaches born, and what are their strengths and weaknesses?
  8. 这台厨房机器人，最后该怎么搭？In the end, how should this kitchen robot be put together?
  • 中间是这台机器人的侧面示意图：手臂、头部相机、底盘前面的雷达，底盘里的 Franka 控制箱和三台计算机（Thor、实时控制电脑、单片机），还有用 Wi-Fi 连着的工作站；每根线标着它是哪种总线。In the middle is a schematic side view of the robot: the arm, the head camera, the lidar at the front of the base, the Franka control box and the three computers in the base (the Thor, the real-time PC and the microcontroller), plus the workstation connected over Wi-Fi; every line is labelled with the kind of bus it is.
  • 线上跑着的小点就是一条条消息，颜色按发送它的那一层，按真实的频率发出，大小按字节数（对数）画。速度 的 1×、1/10、1/100 把时间放慢（默认 1/10）：到 1/100 才看得清手臂那 1 毫秒一个的数据包。下面一把 100 毫秒的尺子，标着每种消息在这 100 毫秒里出现几次。The small dots running along the lines are the individual messages: coloured by the layer that sends them, sent at their real rates, and sized by their byte count (on a log scale). The Speed buttons 1×, 1/10 and 1/100 slow time down (1/10 by default): only at 1/100 can you make out the arm’s packets, one every 1 ms. Below is a 100 ms ruler, marked with how many times each kind of message appears in those 100 ms.
  • 点一个设备或一根线，卡片里写出它走哪种总线、每秒几次、一条多大、每秒多少 MB，以及哪个程序在读它（话题名和消息类型）。Tap a device or a line and a card tells you which bus it uses, how many times a second, how big each message is, how many MB per second, and which program reads it (topic name and message type).
