The readouts keep a running count of the messages and data per second, the fastest and slowest loops, how many compute units and how many programs there are (in the data per second, the size of the arm’s packets is an estimate).

先玩：调到 1/100 看一会儿：相机两帧之间，手臂和控制电脑交换了多少次数据？每秒的数据量里，哪个设备占了九成以上？点一下雷达：它的数据走哪根线，进了哪个程序？Try first: Set the speed to 1/100 and watch for a while: between two camera frames, how many times do the arm and the control computer exchange data? Of the data per second, which device accounts for over 90 percent? Tap the lidar: which line does its data travel along, and which program does it go into?

这一步的要点：一台机器人是十几个设备、几种总线、三四台计算机和二三十个程序拼起来的；最快的回路 1 毫秒一圈，最慢的 100 毫秒，最小的消息几十字节，最大的一帧图近 3 MB。要让它们互相找到、说同一种格式、按时、能启停、能看见、能录下来、能替换，就需要一套统一管理的办法。下面从最底下的总线讲起。The point of this step: A robot is a dozen or so devices, several kinds of bus, three or four computers and twenty or thirty programs pieced together; the fastest loop goes round once every 1 ms and the slowest once every 100 ms, the smallest messages are tens of bytes and the biggest, a single image, is nearly 3 MB. To make them find each other, use one shared format, keep time, start and stop, be seen, be recorded and be replaced, you need one unified way of managing them. Below, we start from the buses at the very bottom.

第 ① 步 · 最底下Step ① · At the very bottom

传感器、总线和驱动：字节怎样进到内存Sensors, buses and drivers: how bytes get into memory

从一帧相机图说起。相机里的芯片把一帧 1280 × 720 的彩色图排成一串字节，切成一个个小包，顺着 USB 线送出去；Thor 上的 USB 控制器收到这些包，不经过 CPU，直接把它们写进内存里事先划好的一块地方（这叫 DMA，直接内存访问）；写完一批，控制器发一个中断，CPU 停下手里的事，跑一小段内核里的 USB 驱动代码；最后，这些小包要拼回一帧完整的图：相机厂家的库 librealsense（ROS 里的相机驱动 realsense2_camera 就建在它上面）走内核的 V4L2 接口时，由内核里的 uvcvideo 驱动来拼；走 libusb 时，由 librealsense 自己在用户态拼。彩色图从相机出来是 YUYV 格式，librealsense 还要把它转成 RGB，realsense2_camera 再把整帧发成 ROS 消息。到这一步为止，和 ROS 一点关系都没有：总线、DMA、中断、内核驱动，全是硬件和 Linux 的事。Let’s start with one camera image. The chip in the camera lays out a 1280 × 720 colour image as a string of bytes, cuts it into small packets and sends them down the USB cable; the USB controller on the Thor receives these packets and, without involving the CPU, writes them straight into a region of memory set aside in advance (this is called DMA, direct memory access); when a batch has been written, the controller raises an interrupt, and the CPU stops what it is doing to run a short piece of the kernel’s USB driver code; finally, the small packets have to be put back together into one complete image: when the camera maker’s library, librealsense (the ROS camera driver realsense2_camera is built on top of it), goes through the kernel’s V4L2 interface, the uvcvideo driver in the kernel does the assembling; when it goes through libusb, librealsense does it itself, in user space. The colour image comes out of the camera in YUYV format; librealsense still has to convert it to RGB, and realsense2_camera then publishes the whole frame as a ROS message. Up to this point, ROS has had nothing at all to do with it: the bus, DMA, interrupts and kernel drivers are all the business of the hardware and Linux.

这台机器人上有好几种总线，各有各的脾气：This robot has quite a few kinds of bus, each with its own temperament:

  • USB：相机走的 USB 3.1 Gen 1 名义上每秒 5 Gbit（USB 3.0），带宽大；但它是电脑一方说了算，设备只能等着被问，线也不能太长。适合把大量数据从身边的设备搬进一台电脑。USB: the camera’s USB 3.1 Gen 1 is nominally 5 Gbit/s (USB 3.0), plenty of bandwidth; but the computer is the one in charge: a device can only wait to be asked, and the cable cannot be very long. It suits moving large amounts of data from nearby devices into one computer.
  • 以太网：雷达和手臂都用网线。百兆网（100BASE-TX）每秒 100 Mbit，千兆网 1 Gbit；数据装在一个个帧里，每帧最多带 1500 字节，多台设备可以经交换机连在一起。可交换机会让帧排队，送到的时刻不完全确定；Franka 也建议，能直连就把控制电脑直接插在控制箱（Control）的网口上，中间别接交换机，而且插的必须是控制箱的网口，不是手臂上的（Franka 文档）。Ethernet: the lidar and the arm both use network cables. 100-megabit Ethernet (100BASE-TX) carries 100 Mbit/s, Gigabit Ethernet 1 Gbit/s; data travels in frames, each carrying at most 1500 bytes, and several devices can be connected together through a switch. But a switch can make frames queue, so the moment they arrive is not entirely predictable; Franka also advises that, where you can, you plug the control computer straight into the network port on the control box (Control), with no switch in between, and that it must be the control box’s port, not the one on the arm (Franka docs).
  • CAN：1986 年博世为汽车做的总线，经典 CAN 每秒最多 1 Mbit，一帧最多只装 8 个字节（CAN 总线）。它慢，但抗干扰、便宜，而且几台设备同时要发时，按帧的编号定优先级，最要紧的那一帧一定先过去。底盘的轮子驱动器就挂在上面。CAN: the bus Bosch made for cars in 1986; classic CAN tops out at 1 Mbit/s, and a frame carries at most 8 bytes (CAN bus). It is slow, but resistant to interference and cheap, and when several devices want to send at the same time, priority goes by the frame’s ID number, so the most urgent frame always gets through first. The base’s wheel drivers sit on it.
  • 串口：最老的一种，比如每秒 115,200 波特，一个字节连起止位一共 10 位，每秒约 11.5 kB。单片机常用它和大电脑说话：中间隔着一块 USB 转串口芯片时（Linux 里常见的是 /dev/ttyUSB0），受这个波特率限制；单片机直接用自己的 USB 口装成串口时（/dev/ttyACM0），速度由 USB 决定，设的波特率不起作用。这台机器人的底盘单片机走的是后一种。Serial: the oldest kind, for example at 115,200 baud, where one byte plus its start and stop bits makes 10 bits in all, about 11.5 kB per second. Microcontrollers often use it to talk to a bigger computer: with a USB-to-serial chip in between (on Linux it is usually /dev/ttyUSB0), the link is limited by that baud rate; when the microcontroller uses its own USB port to pose as a serial port (/dev/ttyACM0), the speed is set by USB, and the baud rate you set has no effect. The base’s microcontroller on this robot uses the second kind.

一条消息在线上要走多久How long a message spends on the wire

t = 8 (L + h · ⌈L / p⌉) / B

一条 L 字节的消息，要切成 ⌈L / p⌉ 帧，每帧再包上 h 字节的包装；全部换成比特，除以总线每秒能传的比特数，就是它在线上要走的时间。A message of L bytes is cut into ⌈L / p⌉ frames, and each frame is wrapped in h bytes of overhead; convert it all to bits, divide by the number of bits the bus can carry per second, and that is the time it spends on the wire.

总线从来不一口气传任意长的数据：每一帧都要带上地址、长度、校验，有的还要在帧和帧之间留一段空。消息越小，包装占的比例越大；总线越慢，每一帧花的时间越长。所以同一条消息，在不同的总线上走的时间可以差上万倍，有的回路在某种总线上根本跑不起来。A bus never carries data of any length in one go: every frame has to carry an address, a length and a checksum, and some buses also leave a gap between one frame and the next. The smaller the message, the bigger the share taken by overhead; the slower the bus, the longer each frame takes. So the time the same message spends on different buses can differ by a factor of more than 10,000, and some loops simply cannot run on certain buses.

t
这条消息在线上要走的时间the time this message spends on the wire
L
消息本身的字节数the size of the message itself, in bytes
p
一帧最多装多少字节的数据：经典 CAN 是 8，以太网上的 UDP 包是 1472the most data bytes one frame can carry: 8 for classic CAN, 1472 for a UDP packet over Ethernet
h
每一帧的包装字节数；以太网是 38 字节（前导码 8、帧头 14、校验 4、帧间隔 12）加上 IP 和 UDP 的头 28 字节，共 66；经典 CAN 是 44 比特，也就是 5.5 字节the overhead bytes per frame; for Ethernet, 38 bytes (preamble 8, header 14, checksum 4, inter-frame gap 12) plus 28 bytes of IP and UDP headers, 66 in all; for classic CAN, 44 bits, that is, 5.5 bytes
B
总线的带宽，单位比特每秒the bandwidth of the bus, in bits per second
⌈x⌉
向上取整：8648 / 1472 ≈ 5.9，要 6 帧round up: 8648 / 1472 ≈ 5.9, so 6 frames

三笔账（我们按上面的式子算的）。CAN：一帧装 8 字节、连包装一共 108 比特（还没算填充位和帧间 3 比特的空隙），在 1 Mbit/s 上走 108 µs。假设七个关节每 1 毫秒各要一帧指令、一帧状态，就是 14 帧、1512 比特、1.512 毫秒，比 1 毫秒还长：一条经典 CAN 带不动七个关节的 1 kHz 回路。千兆以太网：一个 1538 字节的帧里只有 1472 字节是数据，效率 95.7%，每秒最多约 119.6 MB；要是把相机的两个 ROS 话题原样经千兆网发给另一台电脑（彩色图按 ROS 里的 RGB8，一帧 2,764,800 字节），彩色加深度每秒 138.2 MB，放不下：一帧彩色图在线上要 23.1 毫秒，一帧深度图 15.4 毫秒，加起来 38.5 毫秒，可两帧之间只有 33.3 毫秒。就算改发相机自己的 YUYV（合起来每秒 110.6 MB），也要占掉这根线的九成多。雷达：按 ROS 里一圈扫描消息的大小（8,648 字节）算，在百兆网上要 6 帧、0.72 毫秒，每秒 40 圈只占这根线的 2.9%（雷达在网线上用的是厂家自己的协议，字节数和这不完全一样，这里只看量级）。Three calculations (we did them with the formula above). CAN: a frame carrying 8 bytes is 108 bits in all with its overhead (not yet counting bit stuffing or the 3-bit gap between frames), which takes 108 µs at 1 Mbit/s. Suppose each of the seven joints needs one command frame and one state frame every 1 ms: that is 14 frames, 1512 bits, 1.512 ms, longer than the 1 ms itself: a single classic CAN bus cannot carry a 1 kHz loop for seven joints. Gigabit Ethernet: in a 1538-byte frame only 1472 bytes are data, an efficiency of 95.7%, so at most about 119.6 MB/s; if you sent the camera’s two ROS topics unchanged over Gigabit Ethernet to another computer (the colour image as RGB8, the ROS format: 2,764,800 bytes a frame), colour plus depth comes to 138.2 MB/s, which does not fit: one colour image takes 23.1 ms on the wire and one depth image 15.4 ms, 38.5 ms together, yet there are only 33.3 ms between two frames. Even if you sent the camera’s own YUYV instead (110.6 MB/s together), it would still take up just over 90 percent of the cable. Lidar: taking the size of one ROS scan message (8,648 bytes), it needs 6 frames and 0.72 ms on 100-megabit Ethernet, and 40 scans a second take only 2.9% of the cable (on the cable the lidar speaks the maker’s own protocol, so the byte count is not exactly the same; here we only care about the order of magnitude).

这一层的账决定了后面很多"架构"上的选择：相机必须直接插在处理它的那台电脑上，想把画面传给 Wi-Fi 那头的工作站就得先压缩；七个关节要 1 kHz 来回，一条经典 CAN 不够，得分几条或者换更快的总线（Franka 的关节总线藏在手臂和控制箱里面，我们碰得到的 FCI 是控制电脑到控制箱的一根以太网直连线）；1 毫秒的回路，最好只走这种直连的线，不经过交换机、Wi-Fi 或别的电脑。The arithmetic at this layer decides many of the "architectural" choices later on: the camera has to be plugged straight into the computer that processes it, and to send its pictures to the workstation on the other side of the Wi-Fi you must compress them first; for seven joints going back and forth at 1 kHz, one classic CAN bus is not enough, so you have to split them over several buses or move to a faster bus (Franka’s joint bus is hidden inside the arm and the control box; the part we can get at, FCI, is one direct Ethernet cable from the control computer to the control box); a 1 ms loop is best kept on a direct cable like this, without passing through a switch, Wi-Fi or another computer.

字节进了内存以后，在 Linux 里有几种"门牌"：USB 相机可以是 /dev/video0（内核的 V4L2 驱动），网线上的设备就是一个普通的网络套接字，CAN 在 Linux 里是一张叫 can0 的"网卡"（SocketCAN），串口是 /dev/ttyACM0、/dev/ttyUSB0 这样的文件。所谓"ROS 驱动"，其实大多是一个用户态的普通程序：它从这些门牌里读出字节，按厂家的协议解出意思，再换成大家约定好的格式发出去。雷达的 urg_node、相机的 realsense2_camera 都是这样；手臂这边读写字节的是 libfranka，一个被链进控制程序里的库。Once the bytes are in memory, Linux has a few kinds of "address" for them: a USB camera can be /dev/video0 (the kernel’s V4L2 driver), a device on a network cable is just an ordinary network socket, CAN on Linux is a "network card" called can0 (SocketCAN), and a serial port is a file such as /dev/ttyACM0 or /dev/ttyUSB0. A so-called "ROS driver" is mostly an ordinary user-space program: it reads bytes from these addresses, decodes what they mean according to the vendor’s protocol, and sends them out again in the format everyone has agreed on. The lidar’s urg_node and the camera’s realsense2_camera both work this way; on the arm’s side, the bytes are read and written by libfranka, a library linked into the control program.

  • 上面一排选一种总线：USB 3.1 Gen 1、千兆以太网、百兆以太网、CAN（经典）、CAN FD、串口；旁边的小表写着它的带宽、每帧能装多少字节、每帧的包装。In the top row, pick a bus: USB 3.1 Gen 1, Gigabit Ethernet, 100BASE-TX, classic CAN, CAN FD, UART; the small table next to it gives its bandwidth, how many bytes a frame can carry and the overhead per frame.
  • 第二排选一条消息：7 关节指令（7 × 8 字节，还有同样大的状态要传回来）、雷达一圈（8,648 字节）、一帧彩色图（按 ROS 里的 RGB8，2,764,800 字节）、一帧深度图（1,843,200 字节）、彩色 + 深度、IMU 一个采样（24 字节）。In the second row, pick a message: 7-joint command (7 × 8 bytes, plus a state of the same size coming back), one lidar scan (8,648 bytes), one RGB frame (as RGB8, the ROS format: 2,764,800 bytes), one depth frame (1,843,200 bytes), RGB + depth, one IMU sample (24 bytes).
  • 画面分四行：① 消息切成几帧；② 放大一帧，看包装和数据各占多少；③ 一帧接一帧放慢着走上线；④ 和它的周期比，线要忙多久，超出的标红。▶ 播放、上一步、下一步、重来 一行行走过去。下面把数代进上面的式子，读数写出一条消息在线上走多久、每个周期几帧、每秒最多能传几条、要传和能传的数据量、线忙几成，结论是放得下还是放不下。The picture has four rows: ① how many frames the message is cut into; ② one frame enlarged, to see how much of it is overhead and how much is data; ③ the frames going onto the wire one after another, in slow motion; ④ how long the wire is busy compared with the message’s period, with any overrun marked in red. ▶ Play, Back, Next step and Restart walk through them row by row. Below, the numbers are put into the formula above, and the readouts give how long one message spends on the wire, how many frames per period, at most how many messages per second, the data needed and the capacity, what fraction of the time the wire is busy, and the verdict: it fits or it does not fit.
  • 最后"⑤ 到了电脑里"一栏，按顺序列出这种总线的数据进到程序之前经过的每一站：控制器、DMA、中断、内核驱动、用户态驱动程序。线上的时间只算在线上走的那一段，不算排队和驱动的时间。The last panel, "⑤ Inside the computer", lists in order every stop this bus’s data passes through before it reaches a program: the controller, DMA, the interrupt, the kernel driver, the user-space driver program. The time on the wire counts only the stretch spent travelling on the wire, not queueing or driver time.

先玩：选"CAN（经典）"和"7 关节指令"：1 kHz 来回一趟要多久，够吗？换成"千兆以太网"和"彩色 + 深度"：每 33.3 毫秒这根线要忙多久？只送彩色图呢？再选"百兆以太网"和"雷达一圈"：一圈占了这根线的几成？Try first: Pick "classic CAN" and "7-joint command": how long does one round trip at 1 kHz take, and is that enough? Switch to "Gigabit Ethernet" and "RGB + depth": in every 33.3 ms, how long is the wire busy? And with the colour image alone? Then pick "100BASE-TX" and "one lidar scan": what fraction of the wire does one scan take up?

    这一步的要点：最底下是总线、DMA、中断和内核驱动，这些都是硬件和 Linux 的事，不是 ROS 的。一条消息在线上的时间 t = 8 (L + h · ⌈L / p⌉) / B，不同的总线差上万倍：经典 CAN 带不动七个关节的 1 kHz 回路，千兆网带不动 RGB8 的相机流。所谓"ROS 驱动"，大多是一个从 Linux 的设备文件或套接字里读字节、再翻译成统一格式的普通程序。The point of this step: At the very bottom are buses, DMA, interrupts and kernel drivers, all of them the business of the hardware and Linux, not of ROS. The time a message spends on the wire is t = 8 (L + h · ⌈L / p⌉) / B, and different buses differ by a factor of more than 10,000: classic CAN cannot carry a 1 kHz loop for seven joints, and Gigabit Ethernet cannot carry the RGB8 camera stream. A so-called "ROS driver" is mostly an ordinary program that reads bytes from a Linux device file or socket and translates them into one shared format.

    第 ② 步 · 一台电脑上Step ② · On one computer

    进程之间怎么传数据How processes pass data to each other

    相机驱动拿到了一帧图，可要用这帧图的是另一个程序：目标检测。上一篇讲过，每个进程有自己的页表，看到的是自己的一套内存（上一篇第 ② 步）；检测程序没法直接去读相机驱动的内存。这堵墙是好事：一个程序崩了，不会把别的程序的数据写坏。可它也意味着，两个程序之间每传一条消息，要么请内核帮忙搬，要么事先和内核商量好一块两边都看得见的内存。The camera driver has a frame, but the program that needs it is a different one: object detection. As the previous page explained, every process has its own page table and sees a set of memory of its own (step ② of the previous page); the detector cannot simply read the camera driver’s memory. This wall is a good thing: if one program crashes, it cannot corrupt another program’s data. But it also means that for every message two programs pass between them, either the kernel has to move it for them, or they have to arrange with the kernel beforehand a piece of memory that both of them can see.

    办法有这么几种，各有各的代价：There are a few ways to do this, each with its own cost:

    • 全放进一个进程：几个线程共用同一套内存，交一帧图只要交一个指针，几乎不花时间。代价是：一个线程崩了，整个进程一起倒；大家得用同一种语言、一起编译、一起重启。早年很多机器人软件就是这样一个大程序（下一步会讲）。Put everything in one process: the threads share one set of memory, so handing over a frame only means handing over a pointer, which takes almost no time. The cost: if one thread crashes, the whole process goes down with it, and everything has to be in the same language, compiled together and restarted together. A lot of early robot software was one big program like this (the next step covers it).
    • 管道：内核里的一小段缓冲区，一头写、一头读。发送方调用 write() 把数据拷进内核，接收方调用 read() 再拷出来：拷两遍，外加几次系统调用和一次叫醒对方。Pipe: a small buffer in the kernel, written at one end and read at the other. The sender calls write() to copy the data into the kernel, and the receiver calls read() to copy it out again: two copies, plus a few system calls and one wake-up of the other side.
    • 套接字：用法和管道差不多，但更通用。Unix 套接字只在本机用；TCP、UDP 套接字在本机走"回环"，换一个地址就能连到另一台电脑。一套写法本机、跨机都能用，所以 ROS 1 的话题默认全走 TCP。Socket: used much like a pipe, but more general. A Unix socket works only within one machine; TCP and UDP sockets go through the "loopback" on the same machine, and with a different address they connect to another computer. The same code works on one machine and across machines, which is why ROS 1 topics all go over TCP by default.
    • 共享内存：两个进程把同一块物理内存映射进各自的页表，一方写进去，另一方马上看得见，内核不用来回拷。但"我写好了"这件事还得另外通知对方（比如写一下 eventfd，让内核把它叫醒），两边还要自己约好谁什么时候能写、什么时候能读。Shared memory: two processes map the same piece of physical memory into their own page tables, so what one writes the other sees at once, and the kernel does not have to copy anything back and forth. But "I’ve finished writing" still has to be signalled to the other side separately (for example by writing to an eventfd so that the kernel wakes it up), and the two sides have to agree between themselves who may write when and who may read when.

    还有一件事绕不开：序列化。在 C++ 程序里，一条关节状态消息（sensor_msgs/JointState）是一个对象：七个关节的名字是七个字符串，位置、速度、力矩是三个数组，它们各自待在内存的不同地方，靠指针串起来。指针只在本进程里有意义，原样发过去，对方拿到的只是一些没用的地址。所以发送前要把它"排平"：先写数组有多长，再一个个写数据，排成一串连续的字节；接收方按同样的约定再拆回一个对象。两边必须对"有哪些字段、什么类型、什么顺序"一字不差地达成一致，这正是后面 ROS 的消息类型要管的事。ROS 1 用的是自己定的简单格式，ROS 2 经过 DDS 时用 DDS 标准里的 CDR 格式。图像这种大块数据，排平基本上就是整块拷一遍；在 Python 里还要多转一道（第 ⑫ 步算这笔账）。One more thing cannot be avoided: serialisation. In a C++ program, a joint-state message (sensor_msgs/JointState) is an object: the seven joint names are seven strings, and the positions, velocities and torques are three arrays, each living somewhere different in memory, tied together by pointers. A pointer only means something inside its own process: send it across as it is, and the other side gets nothing but useless addresses. So before sending, the message has to be "flattened": first write how long an array is, then write its data item by item, laid out as one continuous run of bytes; the receiver, following the same convention, takes it apart into an object again. Both sides must agree to the letter on "which fields, of which types, in which order", and that is exactly what ROS’s message types will take care of later. ROS 1 uses a simple format of its own; ROS 2, when it goes through DDS, uses the CDR format from the DDS standard. For big blocks of data such as images, flattening basically means copying the whole block once; in Python there is one more conversion on top (step ⑫ works out the cost).

    跨电脑就只剩网络一条路：Thor 和工作站之间是 Wi-Fi 上的 UDP 或 TCP。这时上一步的 t（线上的时间）和下面的 c 要加在一起算。Between computers, the network is the only route: between the Thor and the workstation, it is UDP or TCP over Wi-Fi. Then the previous step’s t (the time on the wire) and the c below have to be added together.

    交一条消息要花多久How long it takes to hand over one message

    c ≈ c0 + k · L / β

    把一条 L 字节的消息交给同一台电脑上的另一个进程，花的时间大约是一个固定的部分 c0，加上把这些字节拷 k 遍的时间；拷一遍要 L / β。Handing a message of L bytes to another process on the same computer takes roughly a fixed part, c0, plus the time to copy those bytes k times; one copy takes L / β.

    交一条消息有两种开销。一种和消息多大无关：系统调用要进出内核，接收方多半在睡觉，要内核把它叫醒、排上 CPU。另一种和字节数成正比：每拷一遍，就要把所有字节读一遍、写一遍。小消息几乎只付第一种，大消息主要付第二种，所以治法也不一样：小消息要少叫醒对方，大消息要少拷。Handing over a message has two kinds of cost. One has nothing to do with the size of the message: system calls have to go into the kernel and back out, and the receiver is most likely asleep, so the kernel has to wake it and get it onto a CPU. The other is proportional to the number of bytes: every copy reads all the bytes once and writes them once. Small messages pay almost only the first kind, big messages mostly the second, so the remedies differ too: for small messages, wake the other side less often; for big ones, copy less.

    c
    交一条消息花的时间the time it takes to hand over one message
    c0
    固定开销：系统调用、叫醒对方、调度，和 L 无关the fixed cost: system calls, waking the other side and scheduling, independent of L
    k
    拷贝的遍数：管道、套接字是 2（拷进内核、再拷出来），共享内存"拷进去"是 1，"原地交出"是 0the number of copies: 2 for pipes and sockets (into the kernel, then out again), 1 for shared memory "copy in", 0 for "in place"
    L
    消息的字节数the size of the message in bytes
    β
    拷贝的速度，单位字节每秒the copying speed, in bytes per second

    我们测的是往返：送过去，对方把数据读一遍，再回 1 个字节，记下整个往返的时间，取中位数；所以下面的 c、c0 都按一个来回算，c0 里也含回答那一次叫醒。64 字节的小消息，五种办法的往返都在 22–31 µs，几乎全是 c0：去、回各叫醒对方一次，每次约 11 µs（我们这台是虚拟机，叫醒一次比真机贵）。一张 2,764,800 字节的图，拷一遍（memcpy）我们测得 224 µs，也就是 β ≈ 12 GB/s。按式子，Unix 套接字拷两遍，c ≈ 22 + 2 × 224 = 470 µs，测得 526 µs；共享内存原地交出，不拷，c ≈ 22 µs，测得 107 µs，多出来的约 85 µs 是接收方把整张图摸一遍（每 64 字节读 1 个字节）的时间；我们的程序每轮只改图的第 1 个字节，图一直待在缓存里，所以这是最好的情况，真换一帧新图会读得更慢。管道最慢，2,069 µs：它在内核里的缓冲区默认只有 64 KiB，一张图得分 43 轮送，每轮都要叫醒对方，c0 付了几十遍。这主要怪缓冲区大小，不怪管道本身：我们给 Unix 套接字设了 4 MiB 的缓冲（默认约 208 KiB，也得分十几轮），管道却用的默认值；用 fcntl 把管道调到 1 MiB，就只要 3 轮。共享内存"拷进去"测得 501 µs，比式子估的多，多半是刚写进去的数据还在发送方那个核的缓存里，接收方读时要从那边搬过来（这是我们的推测，没有再细测）。What we measured is the round trip: we send the message, the other side reads the data once and answers with 1 byte, and we record the time of the whole round trip and take the median. So c and c0 below are both for one round trip, and c0 also includes the wake-up for the answer. For a small 64-byte message, the round trip is 22–31 µs for all five methods, almost all of it c0: one wake-up each way, about 11 µs each (ours is a virtual machine, where a wake-up costs more than on real hardware). For an image of 2,764,800 bytes, we measured one copy (memcpy) at 224 µs, that is, β ≈ 12 GB/s. By the formula, a Unix socket copies twice, c ≈ 22 + 2 × 224 = 470 µs, and we measured 526 µs. With shared memory in place, nothing is copied, c ≈ 22 µs, and we measured 107 µs. The extra 85 µs or so is the time the receiver takes to touch the whole image once (reading 1 byte in every 64). Our program changes only the first byte of the image each round, so the image stays in the cache all along: this is the best case, and a genuinely new frame would be slower to read. The pipe is the slowest, at 2,069 µs: its buffer in the kernel is only 64 KiB by default, so an image has to go across in 43 rounds, each one waking the other side, and c0 is paid several dozen times. That is mostly down to the buffer size, not the pipe itself: we gave the Unix socket a 4 MiB buffer (the default, about 208 KiB, would also take a dozen or so rounds), but left the pipe at its default; set the pipe to 1 MiB with fcntl, and it needs only 3 rounds. Shared memory "copy in" measured 501 µs, more than the formula estimates, most likely because the freshly written data is still in the cache of the sender’s core and has to be fetched from there when the receiver reads it (this is our guess; we did not measure it further).

    同一台电脑上，小消息的代价主要是"叫醒"，大消息的代价主要是"拷贝"。后面会看到，ROS 2 的好几样设计就是冲着这两样去的：把几个节点放进同一个进程、只交指针（组件和进程内通信，第 ⑥ 步），或者让发送方直接把数据写进共享内存（零拷贝，第 ⑤ 步）。On one computer, small messages pay mostly for the "wake-up" and big messages mostly for the "copy". As we will see, several of ROS 2’s design choices are aimed squarely at these two: putting several nodes into one process and handing over only a pointer (components and intra-process communication, step ⑥), or letting the sender write the data straight into shared memory (zero copy, step ⑤).

    • 上面是用户态：左边是发送方 camera_driver，右边是接收方 detector，各有各的内存（用共享内存时，下面多出一块两边都映射了的共享区）；最下面是两个进程共用的 Linux 内核，里面画着管道的缓冲、套接字的队列或者 eventfd。中间那条橙色虚线是系统调用线，每穿过一次就是一次系统调用。At the top is user space: on the left the sender, camera_driver, on the right the receiver, detector, each with its own memory (with shared memory, an extra shared region mapped by both appears below them); at the bottom is the Linux kernel the two processes share, showing the pipe’s buffer, the socket’s queue or the eventfd. The dashed orange line in the middle is the system-call line: every crossing is one system call.
    • 上面一排选办法：管道、Unix 套接字、TCP 回环、共享内存（拷进去）、共享内存（原地交出）；第二排选消息大小：64 B、4 KiB、64 KiB、1 MiB、一帧图 2.76 MB。The top row picks the method: Pipe, Unix socket, TCP loopback, Shared memory (copy in), Shared memory (in place); the second row picks the message size: 64 B, 4 KiB, 64 KiB, 1 MiB, one image 2.76 MB.
    • ▶ 播放 看一轮往返怎么走，或者用 上一步、下一步 一步步看（上面一排小标签也能直接点），重来 回到开头。数据被拷一遍，就有一块从一边挪到另一边；青色的箭头是内核叫醒对方。管道送大消息时，会一轮轮地数给你看。▶ Play shows how one round trip goes, or use Back and Next step to go through it step by step (you can also tap the small labels in the row above directly); Restart goes back to the beginning. Each time the data is copied, a block moves from one side to the other; the teal arrows are the kernel waking the other side. When a pipe carries a big message, the rounds are counted out for you one by one.
    • 读数：到这一步为止拷了几遍、做了几次系统调用、叫醒了几次（斜线后面是一整个往返的总数），我们测的往返中位数和 p99（100 次里最慢的那 1 次大约多慢），以及折算出来每秒能交多少 GB。Readouts: how many copies, system calls and wake-ups there have been up to this step (the number after the slash is the total for a whole round trip), our measured median round trip and p99 (roughly how slow the slowest 1 in 100 is), and what that works out to in GB handed over per second.
    • 最下面的条形图把五种办法在同一个大小下并排比：每根条分成固定的部分 c0（用 64 B 时测的时间）和随大小增长的部分，细线标出 p99；点一行就换到那种办法。The bar chart at the bottom compares the five methods side by side at the same size: each bar is split into the fixed part c0 (the time measured at 64 B) and the part that grows with size, and a thin line marks the p99; tap a row to switch to that method.

    先玩：先用默认的管道和"一帧图 2.76 MB"一步步走一遍：它要分几轮、叫醒几次？再看条形图：五种办法最快和最慢差几倍？最后选"64 B"，五种办法还差得多吗？这时时间花在哪了？Try first: Start with the default pipe and "one image 2.76 MB" and step through it once: how many rounds does it take, and how many wake-ups? Then look at the bar chart: how many times faster is the fastest of the five methods than the slowest? Finally pick "64 B": are the five methods still far apart? Where does the time go now?

    这一步的要点：进程之间隔着一堵墙，传数据要么请内核拷（管道、套接字），要么共用一块内存再另行通知（共享内存），要么干脆放进同一个进程。交一条消息的时间 c ≈ c0 + k · L / β：小消息贵在叫醒对方（我们测得往返约 22 µs），大消息贵在拷贝（一帧图拷一遍 224 µs）。传之前还得把对象排平成字节，两边对格式的约定必须一字不差。The point of this step: Processes are separated by a wall, so passing data means either asking the kernel to copy it (pipes, sockets), or sharing a piece of memory and signalling separately (shared memory), or simply putting everything into one process. Handing over one message takes c ≈ c0 + k · L / β: small messages are expensive because of waking the other side (we measured a round trip of about 22 µs), big ones because of copying (one copy of a frame takes 224 µs). Before sending, an object also has to be flattened into bytes, and the two sides must agree on the format to the letter.

    第 ③ 步 · ROS 以前Step ③ · Before ROS

    每个实验室一套Every lab its own

    前两步的问题，在 ROS 出现以前就全都在：总线要有人写驱动，程序之间要有人约定格式。那时候大致有四种做法，有的到今天还在用。The problems of the last two steps were all there before ROS came along: someone had to write drivers for the buses, and someone had to agree on formats between programs. Back then there were roughly four approaches, and some are still in use today.

    • 厂家的控制柜和厂家的语言：工业机器人买来就带一个控制柜，伺服回路、轨迹插补、安全都在柜子里，用户用厂家自己的语言写动作程序：KUKA 的叫 KRL，ABB 的叫 RAPID。大多数商用工业机器人厂商都要求用自家的专有语言编程；研究者说这些语言常有"跟着控制器走的设计、表达能力有限、没法扩展"的毛病（Mühe 等，2010）。它可靠、确定、经过认证，可想在上面接一个新相机、跑一个学出来的策略，就很难。The vendor’s control cabinet and the vendor’s language: an industrial robot comes with a control cabinet; the servo loops, trajectory interpolation and safety all live in the cabinet, and users write motion programs in the vendor’s own language: KUKA’s is called KRL, ABB’s RAPID. Most commercial makers of industrial robots require their robots to be programmed in their own proprietary language; researchers say these languages often suffer from "controller-specific design, limited expressiveness and a lack of extensibility" (Mühe et al., 2010). It is reliable, deterministic and certified, but hooking up a new camera to it or running a learned policy on it is hard.
    • PLC：工厂里的可编程逻辑控制器，按一个固定的周期反复做三件事：读所有输入、跑一遍程序、写所有输出。编程语言由 IEC 61131-3 统一规定（1993 年 12 月第一版），有梯形图、功能块图、结构化文本、顺序功能图几种（IEC 61131-3）。它极其稳定，适合传送带和气缸，不适合点云和规划。PLC: the programmable logic controller found in factories, which does three things over and over at a fixed period: read all the inputs, run the program once, write all the outputs. Its programming languages are standardised by IEC 61131-3 (first edition December 1993) and come in a few kinds: ladder diagram, function block diagram, structured text and sequential function chart (IEC 61131-3). It is extremely stable, well suited to conveyor belts and pneumatic cylinders, but not to point clouds and planning.
    • 一个大程序：研究室里常见的做法。为一台机器人从头写一个 C 或 C++ 程序，驱动、建图、规划、控制全在一个进程里，靠函数调用和全局变量传数据。快、简单；可换一台机器人就得大改，别的实验室也用不上。One big program: the common approach in research labs. You write one C or C++ program from scratch for one robot, with the drivers, mapping, planning and control all in one process, passing data through function calls and global variables. It is fast and simple; but a different robot means a major rewrite, and other labs cannot use it either.
    • 实验室自己的框架：有人开始把通信和驱动抽出来，做成别人也能用的框架。各自为了自己的问题而生：Player（南加州大学，2001 年开始发布）给各种机器人和传感器一个统一的网络接口，配着 Stage、Gazebo 两个仿真器；OROCOS（2001 年 9 月起的欧盟项目，鲁汶大学牵头）做硬实时的控制和运动学库，它的运动学库 KDL 后来进了 ROS（OROCOS 历史）；CARMEN（卡内基梅隆大学）做移动机器人导航；YARP（2002 年第一次发布，2006 年发表论文）后来成了 iCub 人形机器人的中间件；微软的 Robotics Developer Studio（2006 年 12 月）走 Windows 和 .NET 的路子，2014 年随部门一起停掉（MRDS）；LCM 是麻省理工为 2007 年 DARPA 城市挑战赛的无人车写的，用 UDP 组播、没有中心节点，消息格式写成一份类型说明，再自动生成各种语言的代码（Huang 等，2010）。这些框架的综述见 Tsardoulias 和 Mitkas。Labs’ own frameworks: people began to pull the communication and the drivers out into frameworks that others could use too. Each was born for a problem of its own: Player (University of Southern California, first released in 2001) gave all kinds of robots and sensors one uniform network interface, with two simulators to go with it, Stage and Gazebo; OROCOS (an EU project from September 2001, led by KU Leuven) worked on hard real-time control and kinematics libraries, and its kinematics library, KDL, later went into ROS (OROCOS history); CARMEN (Carnegie Mellon University) did mobile-robot navigation; YARP (first released in 2002, with a paper in 2006) later became the middleware of the iCub humanoid robot; Microsoft’s Robotics Developer Studio (December 2006) took the Windows and .NET route and was shut down in 2014 along with the group behind it (MRDS); LCM was written at MIT for its self-driving car in the 2007 DARPA Urban Challenge: it uses UDP multicast with no central hub, and message formats are written as a type specification from which code for various languages is generated automatically (Huang et al., 2010). For a survey of these frameworks, see Tsardoulias and Mitkas.

    问题出在"各自"两个字上。每个框架有自己的消息格式、自己的工具、自己的小圈子；给 Player 写的驱动，OROCOS 用不上；一个项目的经费结束，框架就慢慢没人维护。后来参与创办 ROS 的 Keenan Wyrobek 回忆，他们问过的机器人博士一遍遍说同一件事：读博四年，拼出一台勉强能动的机器人和一堆代码，拍个视频就结束了；花四年"在做别人早就做过的事"，九成的工作在重复别人做过的东西，他们提不起劲。他们想要的是"让大家能在彼此的成果上接着往上搭"（IEEE Spectrum，2017）。规模一大，这个问题更明显：麻省理工那辆无人车上同时跑着 70 个模块，分布在 10 台联网的工作站上，平均每秒约 6,775 条消息、16.6 MB（Huang 等）。The trouble lies in the words "its own". Each framework had its own message format, its own tools, its own small community; a driver written for Player was no use to OROCOS; and once a project’s funding ended, its framework slowly went unmaintained. Keenan Wyrobek, who later helped found ROS, recalls that the robotics PhDs they talked to said the same thing over and over: four years of a PhD went into piecing together a robot that barely worked and a pile of code, then they made a video, and that was the end of it. Spending four years "doing what someone else had done before", with 90 percent of the work repeating what others had already done, did not appeal to them. What they wanted was to "enable people to build on each other’s results" (IEEE Spectrum, 2017). At scale, the problem becomes even more obvious: MIT’s self-driving car ran 70 modules at once, spread over 10 networked workstations, averaging about 6,775 messages and 16.6 MB a second (Huang et al.).

    接线要几根How many wires it takes

    Kpair = N (N − 1) / 2Kbus = N

    N 个程序两两之间各定一套约定，最多要 N (N − 1) / 2 套；如果大家都说同一种公共格式、挂在同一条公共的"总线"上，每个程序只要一个转接头，一共 N 个。If every pair among N programs sets up its own convention, that takes up to N (N − 1) / 2 of them; if everyone speaks one shared format and hangs on one shared "bus", each program needs just one adapter, N in all.

    从 N 个程序里挑两个，有 N (N − 1) / 2 种挑法；每一对要自己商量格式、地址、谁先连谁。可约定的数量只是一半的麻烦，另一半在改动的时候：两两直连时，换掉一个程序，所有和它说话的程序（最多 N − 1 个）都得跟着改；有一套公共格式时，只要改它自己的那个转接头。公共格式定得越早、用的人越多，这笔账越划算，这也是后来大家愿意忍受 ROS 种种毛病的根本原因。There are N (N − 1) / 2 ways to pick two programs out of N, and each pair has to settle its own format, its addresses and who connects to whom first. But the number of conventions is only half the trouble; the other half comes when things change: wired point-to-point, swapping out one program means that every program talking to it (up to N − 1 of them) has to change too; with one shared format, only that program’s own adapter has to change. The earlier a shared format is settled and the more people use it, the better the deal, and that is the root reason why people later put up with ROS’s many flaws.

    N
    要连在一起的程序个数the number of programs to be connected
    Kpair
    两两直连、各定各的格式时，最多要几套约定how many conventions are needed at most when wiring point-to-point, each pair with its own format
    Kbus
    大家用一套公共格式时，要几个转接头how many adapters are needed when everyone uses one shared format

    N = 8 时，两两直连 8 × 7 / 2 = 28 套，公共格式 8 个；这台厨房机器人约 30 个程序，30 × 29 / 2 = 435 对 30；麻省理工的无人车 70 个模块，70 × 69 / 2 = 2,415 对 70。当然不是每两个程序都要说话，这是最坏的情况；可只要说话的对数随 N 涨得比 N 快，公共格式就越来越划算。At N = 8, point-to-point takes 8 × 7 / 2 = 28 conventions, a shared format 8 adapters; the kitchen robot has about 30 programs: 30 × 29 / 2 = 435 against 30; MIT’s self-driving car had 70 modules: 70 × 69 / 2 = 2,415 against 70. Of course, not every pair of programs needs to talk, so this is the worst case; but as long as the number of pairs that talk grows faster than N, a shared format pays off more and more.

    "公共的总线"在这里不是一根真的线，而是一套大家都认的约定：消息长什么样、怎么找到对方、用什么工具看和录。ROS 后来做的，主要就是这件事。The "shared bus" here is not a real wire but a convention everyone accepts: what messages look like, how to find each other, which tools to view and record them with. That, mostly, is what ROS went on to do.

    • 拖 模块数 N（2 到 30，默认 8），圆圈是程序。两种接法二选一：两两直连，各定各的格式（每对之间一根线）和 一条公共总线，一套公共消息（每个程序一根线连到中间的总线）。Drag Modules N (2 to 30, default 8); the circles are programs. Choose one of two ways of wiring: Point-to-point, each pair its own format (one line between every pair) or One shared bus, one shared set of message types (one line from each program to the bus in the middle).
    • 点 换掉一个相机：两两直连时，和相机相连的线都变红，读数写出要跟着改的程序有几个；接在公共总线上时，只有相机自己的转接头要改。Tap Swap the camera: wired point-to-point, every line connected to the camera turns red, and the readout shows how many programs have to change along with it; on the shared bus, only the camera’s own adapter has to change.
    • MIT 2007 一键把 N 设成 70，看看那辆无人车两两直连要多少根线；再点一下回到原来的 N。MIT 2007 sets N to 70 at a tap, to show how many lines that self-driving car would need wired point-to-point; tap it again to go back to your previous N.
    • ▶ 播放、上一步、下一步、重来：一次加一个（或减一个）程序，新程序带来的线会亮一下；重来回到 N = 2。读数是连接数、换掉相机要改几个程序，以及另一种接法下这两个数是多少；旁边的小图画出 N (N − 1) / 2 和 N 随 N 怎么涨。▶ Play, Back, Next step, Restart: add (or remove) one program at a time, and the lines the new program brings light up for a moment; Restart goes back to N = 2. The readouts are the number of connections, how many programs a camera swap changes, and what these two numbers are with the other wiring; the small chart beside them shows how N (N − 1) / 2 and N grow with N.
    • 下面的时间轴点一个点，看一个 ROS 以前的框架是谁做的、为了解决什么问题。In the timeline below, tap a dot to see who made a pre-ROS framework and what problem it was meant to solve.

    先玩：N = 8 时两种接法各要几根线？换掉一个相机，各要改几个程序？再点 MIT 2007：两两直连还画得清吗？Try first: At N = 8, how many lines does each wiring need? Swap the camera: how many programs does each one have to change? Then tap MIT 2007: can point-to-point still be drawn legibly?

    这一步的要点：ROS 以前，工业界用厂家的控制柜和 PLC，研究界要么写一个大程序，要么用各实验室自己的框架（Player、OROCOS、CARMEN、YARP、MRDS、LCM……）。每个都解决了自己的问题，但格式、工具、驱动互不相通，大家反复做别人做过的事。程序一多，两两约定的数量按 N (N − 1) / 2 涨，一套公共约定只要 N 个转接头。The point of this step: Before ROS, industry used vendors’ control cabinets and PLCs, while researchers either wrote one big program or used each lab’s own framework (Player, OROCOS, CARMEN, YARP, MRDS, LCM …). Each solved its own problem, but their formats, tools and drivers did not work with one another, and people kept redoing what others had already done. With more programs, the number of pairwise conventions grows as N (N − 1) / 2, while one shared convention needs only N adapters.

    第 ④ 步 · ROS 1Step ④ · ROS 1

    一本电话簿和一套约定A phone book and a set of conventions

    ROS 的起点是斯坦福。Morgan Quigley 在吴恩达的 STAIR 机器人项目里写过一个叫 Switchyard 的框架，用来让一个项目里的各个程序配合起来；同在斯坦福的 Eric Berger 和 Keenan Wyrobek 想做一个"大家都能在上面接着搭"的平台。2007 年，Berger 和 Wyrobek 去了门洛帕克的 Willow Garage（Quigley 一直是斯坦福的学生，没在那里上过班），同年 11 月开始做 ROS，同时造一台叫 PR2 的研究机器人，目标是"撑得起接下来五年的软件开发"（IEEE Spectrum，Why ROS 2?）。2009 年的论文把 ROS 的设计目标写成五个词（Quigley 等，2009）：ROS started at Stanford. In Andrew Ng’s STAIR robot project, Morgan Quigley had written a framework called Switchyard to get the programs in a project working together; Eric Berger and Keenan Wyrobek, also at Stanford, wanted to build a platform "that everyone could keep building on". In 2007 Berger and Wyrobek moved to Willow Garage in Menlo Park (Quigley remained a Stanford student throughout and never worked there). That November they started work on ROS, and at the same time built a research robot called the PR2, meant to "support the next five years of software development" (IEEE Spectrum, Why ROS 2?). The 2009 paper sums up ROS’s design goals in five terms (Quigley et al., 2009):

    • 点对点：程序之间直接连，不经过一个中心服务器转发数据，因为 PR2 身上和身边有好几台电脑，大块数据不该绕路。Peer-to-peer: programs connect to each other directly, with no central server relaying the data, because the PR2 had several computers on board and around it, and large chunks of data should not take a detour.
    • 靠工具：不做一个包揽一切的大程序，而是一堆小工具：启动、录包、看图、查话题，各管一件事。Tools-based: instead of one big program that does everything, lots of small tools for launching, recording bags, viewing images and inspecting topics, each doing one job.
    • 多语言：C++、Python，当时还有 Octave 和 LISP。消息格式写在与语言无关的定义文件里，再自动生成各语言的代码。Multi-lingual: C++ and Python, and at the time also Octave and LISP. Message formats are written in language-neutral definition files, from which the code for each language is generated automatically.
    • 薄：鼓励把驱动和算法写成不依赖 ROS 的独立库，ROS 只是外面薄薄的一层包装，这样换框架时库还能用。Thin: drivers and algorithms are encouraged to be written as standalone libraries that do not depend on ROS, with ROS just a thin wrapper around the outside, so the libraries still work if you switch frameworks.
    • 免费、开源：用 BSD 许可，公司拿去做产品也行。Free and open-source: under the BSD licence, so companies can use it in products too.

    落到实处，ROS 1 定了几样东西。一个程序叫一个节点；节点之间按名字交换数据：话题是一条有名字的单向数据流，比如 /scan，上面流的每条消息类型事先定好，谁都可以发布、谁都可以订阅；服务是一问一答，一个服务名只能有一个节点提供；参数是放在公共地方的配置项。还有一个叫 roscore 的主节点，它就是一本电话簿：记着谁发布什么、谁订阅什么，也存着所有参数。注意它只管"介绍"，不管"传话"：In concrete terms, ROS 1 laid down a few things. A program is called a node, and nodes exchange data by name: a topic is a named one-way stream of data, such as /scan, where the type of every message on it is fixed in advance, and anyone can publish and anyone can subscribe; a service is one question and one answer, and only one node can provide a given service name; parameters are configuration items kept in a shared place. There is also a master called roscore, which is simply a phone book: it records who publishes what and who subscribes to what, and it also stores all the parameters. Note that it only "makes introductions"; it does not "carry the conversation":

    1. roscore 启动，在 11311 端口等着（ros_comm 源码）。roscore starts and waits on port 11311 (ros_comm source).
    2. 相机节点 /camera 启动，用 XML-RPC（一种基于 HTTP 的远程调用）告诉主节点：我发布 /camera/color/image_raw，类型 sensor_msgs/Image。The camera node /camera starts and tells the master over XML-RPC (a kind of remote procedure call built on HTTP): I publish /camera/color/image_raw, type sensor_msgs/Image.
    3. 检测节点 /detector 启动，告诉主节点：我订阅这个话题。主节点把所有发布者的地址回给它。The detector node /detector starts and tells the master: I subscribe to this topic. The master replies with the addresses of all the topic’s publishers.
    4. /detector 直接去问 /camera：用 TCPROS 传行不行？/camera 回一个 TCP 端口号。/detector asks /camera directly: can you send it over TCPROS? /camera replies with a TCP port number.
    5. /detector 连上这个端口，先送一个"连接头"：我是谁、要哪个话题、什么类型、类型的指纹（md5sum）是多少。/camera 核对指纹，一致就回自己的连接头。/detector connects to that port and first sends a "connection header": who I am, which topic I want, what type it is, and what the type’s fingerprint (md5sum) is. /camera checks the fingerprint and, if it matches, replies with its own connection header.
    6. 从此每条消息就是"4 字节长度 + 排平的字节"，从 /camera 直接流到 /detector，主节点再也不经手。From then on every message is "a 4-byte length + the flattened bytes", flowing straight from /camera to /detector; the master never touches it again.

    点对点还有一个后果：每多一个订阅者，就多一条 TCP 连接，同一帧图要单独再发一遍。一路 1280 × 720 的彩色图每秒约 82.9 MB，同时被 /detector 和 /rviz 订阅，/camera 每秒就要往外送约 165.9 MB。Peer-to-peer has another consequence: each extra subscriber means one more TCP connection, and the same image frame has to be sent again, separately. A single 1280 × 720 colour image stream is about 82.9 MB per second; with both /detector and /rviz subscribed, /camera has to send out about 165.9 MB every second.

    第 5 步的"指纹"是 ROS 1 检查"两边说的是不是同一种格式"的办法：不比较整份定义，只比较一个 MD5。算法是把消息定义去掉注释和多余的空白，把里面嵌套的类型换成那个类型自己的 MD5，再对这段文字算 MD5。比如 sensor_msgs/Image（其中 Header 那一行先换成 Header 的 MD5）：The "fingerprint" in step 5 is ROS 1’s way of checking "whether both sides speak the same format": rather than comparing the whole definition, it compares a single MD5. The rule is to strip the comments and extra whitespace from the message definition, replace each nested type with that type’s own MD5, and then take the MD5 of the resulting text. For example, sensor_msgs/Image (where the Header line is first replaced by Header’s MD5):

    2176decaecbce78abc3b96ef049fabed header uint32 height uint32 width string encoding uint8 is_bigendian uint32 step uint8[] data → md5 = 060021388200f6f0f447d0fcd9c64743

    （这几个 MD5 是我们按 ROS 1 genmsg 的规则自己算的，和 ROS 1 里的一致。）只要有一边的定义多了一个字段、改了一个名字，指纹就整个变掉，发布方会直接拒绝，日志里是这样一句（rospy 的原话；括号里的值是我们算的：/detector 用的旧定义在 step 后面多了一行 uint32 exposure_us）：(We calculated these MD5s ourselves using ROS 1’s genmsg rules; they match the ones in ROS 1.) If either side’s definition has just one extra field or one renamed field, the whole fingerprint changes and the publisher refuses outright, with a line like this in its log (rospy’s exact wording; we calculated the values in the brackets: the old definition /detector uses has an extra line uint32 exposure_us after the step field):

    Client [/detector] wants topic [/camera/color/image_raw] to have datatype/md5sum [sensor_msgs/Image/5be3ae8a474191e2040e465b6fac6790], but our version has [sensor_msgs/Image/060021388200f6f0f447d0fcd9c64743] Dropping connection.

    这个做法简单、可靠，也很严格：格式不一致就不通，不会读出一堆错的数。它也埋下了后面"升级就坏"的一个原因：两台电脑上同一种消息的定义只要差一个字段，新旧节点之间就连不上（版本的事见第 ⑪ 步）。This approach is simple, reliable and strict: if the formats do not match, nothing gets through, so you never read out a pile of wrong numbers. It also planted one of the causes of the later "upgrade and it breaks": if the definitions of the same message on two computers differ by just one field, old and new nodes cannot connect (for versions, see step ⑪).

    在这套通信之上，ROS 1 长出了一整套工具和软件包：编译用 catkin，一次启动几十个节点用 roslaunch 和一个 XML 文件，录包和回放用 rosbag，三维显示用 rviz，记各坐标系之间关系的用 tf（第 ⑩ 步）。驱动、建图、导航、手臂规划都有人写好了，装上就能用。我们数了官方索引里每个 ROS 1 发行版发布的软件包数：Indigo 2,779 个，Kinetic 2,772 个，Melodic 2,407 个，最后一个发行版 Noetic 2,175 个。这就是上一步说的"公共格式"：一个相机驱动发 sensor_msgs/Image，世界上所有用 ROS 的检测程序都能直接订阅。On top of this communication scheme, ROS 1 grew a whole set of tools and packages: catkin for building, roslaunch and an XML file for starting several dozen nodes at once, rosbag for recording bags and playback, rviz for 3D visualisation, and tf for keeping track of how frames relate to each other (step ⑩). Drivers, mapping, navigation and arm planning had all been written by someone already, ready to use once installed. We counted the packages released for each ROS 1 distribution in the official index: Indigo 2,779, Kinetic 2,772, Melodic 2,407, and the last distribution, Noetic, 2,175. This is the "shared format" from the previous step: a camera driver publishes sensor_msgs/Image, and every detection program in the world that uses ROS can subscribe to it directly.

    PR2 的六个假设The PR2’s six assumptions

    ROS 1 是为 PR2 量身做的，ROS 2 的设计文档把当年默认的前提列了出来（Why ROS 2?）。每一条，后来都成了 ROS 1 做不好的事：ROS 1 was tailor-made for the PR2, and the ROS 2 design document lists the premises it took for granted at the time (Why ROS 2?). Every one of them later became something ROS 1 could not do well:

    • 只有一台机器人。几台机器人一起干活时，只能在"一个主节点"的结构上硬凑。A single robot. With several robots working as a team, the only option is a hack on top of the "one master" structure.
    • 机器人身上有工作站级的电脑。单片机上跑不了 ROS 1，只能经 rosserial 这样的桥接程序挂在一台电脑上，算不上正式的一员。Workstation-class computers on board. A microcontroller cannot run ROS 1; it can only hang off a computer through a bridge program such as rosserial, and never counts as a full member.
    • 不需要实时。1 毫秒一圈的控制回路，ROS 1 的通信给不了保证，只能在它外面另做。No real-time requirements. For a control loop that runs once every 1 ms, ROS 1’s communication offers no guarantee, so such loops have to be built separately, outside ROS 1.
    • 网络很好。话题默认都走 TCP，TCP 保证顺序、丢了就重发；在信号差的 Wi-Fi 上，丢一个包，后面的数据就都得等它，图像越积越旧。An excellent network. Topics all go over TCP by default, and TCP guarantees order and resends anything lost; on Wi-Fi with a poor signal, one lost packet holds up all the data behind it, and the images pile up and get staler and staler.
    • 主要用于研究。产品要的东西它没有：没有身份认证，网上谁都能往话题里发指令；主节点一挂，新节点就找不到别人了。Mainly for research. It lacks what products need: there is no authentication, so anyone on the network can send commands to a topic; and once the master goes down, new nodes cannot find anyone else.
    • 尽量灵活，"不包住你的 main()"。节点什么时候配置、什么时候开始干活，没有统一的规矩，几十个节点按什么顺序起来全靠各写各的。Maximum flexibility: "we don’t wrap your main()". There is no common rule for when a node gets configured or when it starts working, so the order in which several dozen nodes come up depends entirely on what each one’s own code does.
    • Thor 上画着主节点 roscore（http://localhost:11311）和它的登记表：哪个话题、谁发布、谁订阅；旁边是 /camera 和 /detector，Wi-Fi 那头的工作站上还有一个稍后才来的 /rviz。旁边的记录框写出每一步线上实际传了什么。On Thor you see the master roscore (http://localhost:11311) and its registration table: which topic, who publishes, who subscribes; next to it are /camera and /detector, and on the workstation at the other end of the Wi-Fi there is also /rviz, which arrives later. The log box alongside spells out what actually goes over the wire at each step.
    • ▶ 播放、上一步、下一步、重来：一步步看一次订阅怎么接通，前六步对应上面的六步，第 7 步 /rviz 也来订阅。读数：主节点在不在、有几条数据连接（TCPROS）、图像经不经过主节点、/camera 每秒发出多少字节。▶ Play, Back, Next step, Restart: watch step by step how a subscription gets connected; the first six steps match the six above, and in step 7 /rviz subscribes too. Readouts: whether the master is running, how many data connections (TCPROS) there are, whether images pass through the master, and how many bytes /camera sends per second.
    • 关掉主节点：直接跳到接通以后，把主节点停掉，看已有的图像流还在不在；下一步 /rviz 来订阅，看它能不能接上。Kill the master: jumps straight to after the connection is made and stops the master, so you can see whether the existing image stream is still there; at the next step /rviz comes to subscribe: can it connect?
    • 用旧版消息定义：让 /detector 用一份在 step 后面多了一个字段的旧定义，看握手时发生什么。下面的指纹框里可以 加一个字段、改一个名字、加一行注释、还原，指纹当场重算。Old message definition: gives /detector an old definition with one extra field after the step field, so you can see what happens during the handshake. In the fingerprint box below you can Add a field, Rename a field, Add a comment or Restore, and the fingerprint is recalculated on the spot.

    先玩：先一步步走到第 7 步：/rviz 也订阅以后，/camera 每秒要送出多少？再点"关掉主节点"：图还在流吗？/rviz 还能接上吗？最后在指纹框里分别点"加一行注释"和"加一个字段"：指纹变了没有？Try first: Go through to step 7 one step at a time: once /rviz subscribes too, how much does /camera have to send each second? Then press "Kill the master": are the images still flowing? Can /rviz still connect? Finally, in the fingerprint box, press "Add a comment" and "Add a field" one at a time: does the fingerprint change?

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    


    这一步的要点：ROS 1 = 一本电话簿（主节点）+ 一套公共约定（消息类型、话题名）+ 点对点的 TCP 连接 + 一大堆工具和软件包。主节点只负责介绍，数据不经过它；类型靠定义文本的 MD5 核对，差一个字段就不通。它是照着 PR2 的六个假设做的：一台机器人、电脑够强、不要实时、网络好、用于研究、尽量灵活；这六条后来都被现实打破了。The point of this step: ROS 1 = a phone book (the master) + a shared convention (message types, topic names) + peer-to-peer TCP connections + a big pile of tools and packages. The master only makes introductions; the data never passes through it. Types are checked with the MD5 of the definition text, and one differing field is enough to block the connection. It was built around the PR2’s six assumptions: one robot, powerful computers, no real-time, a good network, research use, maximum flexibility; reality later broke all six.
    

    

    

    第 ⑤ 步 · ROS 2Step ⑤ · ROS 2
    

    把通信交给 DDSHanding communication over to DDS
    

    2014 年，ROS 的维护者写了一篇《Why ROS 2?》（设计文档），列出 ROS 1 应付不了的新场合：多台机器人组队；没有操作系统的单片机；实时控制；从信号差的 Wi-Fi 到地面和太空之间那种很差的网络；产品而不是实验室；需要规定好的做法（比如生命周期、静态配置）。为什么不在 ROS 1 上接着改？文档的回答是：要改的地方太深，动一个这么多人在用的系统风险太大，他们希望 ROS 1 照常能用、不受影响。文档另一处还说，很多 ROS 代码一直兼容到 2009 年 2 月的 0.4 版，稳定是稳定，可也一直背着当年并不最好的接口设计，正好借 ROS 2 重新设计。于是 ROS 2 作为一套平行的新软件包从头写起，和 ROS 1 在 API 上不兼容，靠桥接程序共存。2015 年 8 月出了第一个 alpha，2017 年 12 月第一个正式发行版 Ardent（发行版列表）。In 2014 the maintainers of ROS wrote "Why ROS 2?" (design document), listing new situations that ROS 1 could not cope with: teams of several robots; microcontrollers with no operating system; real-time control; poor networks, from Wi-Fi with a weak signal to the very poor links between the ground and space; products rather than the lab; and the need for prescribed ways of doing things (such as lifecycles and static configuration). Why not just keep changing ROS 1? The document’s answer: the changes would go too deep, touching a system that so many people were using was too risky, and they wanted ROS 1 to keep working as it was, unaffected. Elsewhere the document also says that much ROS code had stayed compatible all the way back to version 0.4 from February 2009: that was stable, certainly, but it also meant still carrying interface designs from back then that were not the best, and ROS 2 was a chance to redesign them. So ROS 2 was written from scratch as a parallel set of new packages, with an API that is not compatible with ROS 1, and the two coexist through bridge programs. The first alpha came out in August 2015, and the first official distribution, Ardent, in December 2017 (list of distributions).
    

    同一篇文档还说，ROS 1 的通信"几乎全是从零写的"：发现、消息定义、序列化、传输都是自己做的。2007 年以后，外面已经有了现成的东西，其中一个是 DDS（数据分发服务）：工业界的发布/订阅标准，2004 年 12 月出了 1.0 版（OMG DDS），2008 年 OMG 又发布了线上互通协议 DDSI-RTPS 2.0，让不同厂家的实现能互相说话（DDSI-RTPS）。DDS 本来就有 ROS 1 缺的几样：不要中心的自动发现、可调的服务质量、跑在 UDP 上，还有面向实时和嵌入式的实现。ROS 2 决定不再自己造这一层，而是站在它上面。The same document also says that ROS 1’s communication was "almost entirely built from scratch": discovery, message definitions, serialisation and transport were all done in-house. Since 2007, ready-made options had appeared elsewhere, and one of them is DDS (Data Distribution Service): an industrial publish/subscribe standard whose version 1.0 came out in December 2004 (OMG DDS); in 2008 the OMG also published a wire protocol for interoperability, DDSI-RTPS 2.0, so that implementations from different vendors could talk to each other (DDSI-RTPS). DDS already had several things ROS 1 lacked: automatic discovery with no central server, tunable quality of service, running over UDP, and implementations aimed at real-time and embedded systems. ROS 2 decided to stop building this layer itself and to stand on top of DDS instead.
    

    五层，一层叠一层Five layers, one on top of another
    

    于是你的一个 ROS 2 节点发一条消息，要往下穿过这几层：So when one of your ROS 2 nodes sends a message, it passes down through these layers:
    

      

    • rclcpp 或 rclpy：你写代码时直接用的 C++ 库和 Python 库，提供节点、发布者、订阅者、定时器这些对象。rclcpp or rclpy: the C++ and Python libraries you use directly when writing code; they provide objects such as nodes, publishers, subscriptions and timers.
      • 

    • rcl：一个用 C 写的公共核心，两种语言的库都建在它上面，这样名字规则、参数、时间这些逻辑只写一遍（客户端库）。rcl: a shared core written in C, on which the libraries for both languages are built, so that logic such as naming rules, parameters and time is written only once (client libraries).
      • 

    • rmw：ROS 的"中间件接口"，一组 C 函数：创建发布者、发一条消息、等数据……它只规定要做什么，不管怎么做。rmw: ROS’s "middleware interface", a set of C functions: create a publisher, publish a message, wait for data … It specifies only what has to be done, not how.
      • 

    • rmw 的实现：把这组函数翻译到某个具体的中间件上。Jazzy 和 Lyrical 默认用 rmw_fastrtps_cpp（eProsima 的 Fast DDS）；官方一级支持的还有 rmw_cyclonedds_cpp（Eclipse Cyclone DDS）、rmw_connextdds（RTI Connext），以及 Kilted 起升为一级的 rmw_zenoh_cpp（Eclipse Zenoh，不是 DDS）（REP 2000、Kilted 说明）。换中间件不用改代码，设一个环境变量 RMW_IMPLEMENTATION 就行。默认值也换过：Galactic 把默认改成了 Cyclone DDS，下一个版本 Humble 又改回 Fast DDS。An rmw implementation: maps this set of functions onto one particular middleware. Jazzy and Lyrical use rmw_fastrtps_cpp (eProsima’s Fast DDS) by default; the others with official Tier 1 support are rmw_cyclonedds_cpp (Eclipse Cyclone DDS), rmw_connextdds (RTI Connext) and rmw_zenoh_cpp (Eclipse Zenoh, which is not DDS), promoted to Tier 1 from Kilted on (REP 2000, Kilted release notes). Switching middleware needs no code changes: just set one environment variable, RMW_IMPLEMENTATION. The default has changed too: Galactic made Cyclone DDS the default, and the next distribution, Humble, went back to Fast DDS.
      • 

    • 中间件本身：负责发现、排队、可靠传输，最后把字节交给 UDP 套接字（Zenoh 默认用 TCP），或者同一台电脑上的共享内存。The middleware itself: takes care of discovery, queuing and reliable delivery, and finally hands the bytes to a UDP socket (Zenoh uses TCP by default) or, on the same computer, to shared memory.
      • 

    

    这几层有多大？我们数了源码（不算测试和例子）：rcl 37,280 行 C，rmw 12,546 行，rclcpp 61,993 行 C++，rclpy 26,144 行；而光是 Cyclone DDS 这一个中间件就有 238,823 行（98% 是 C），比上面四个加起来还多。ROS 2 的通信，大部分代码其实不在 ROS 里。How big are these layers? We counted the source (excluding tests and examples): rcl is 37,280 lines of C, rmw 12,546 lines, rclcpp 61,993 lines of C++ and rclpy 26,144 lines; Cyclone DDS alone, just one middleware, has 238,823 lines (98% of it C), more than the four above put together. Most of the code behind ROS 2’s communication is not actually in ROS.
    

    没有电话簿，怎么找到对方No phone book: how do they find each other?
    

    ROS 2 没有主节点。每个 ROS 2 进程在 DDS 里是一个"参与者"；它一启动，就往局域网上组播一句"我在这儿"，别的参与者听到后回应，接着双方交换各自的端点：我写哪个话题、什么类型、什么 QoS；我读哪个话题……话题名、类型都对上、QoS 也兼容，这一对就连上，之后数据走点对点的 UDP（同一台电脑上可以走共享内存）。参与者每隔一段时间再喊一次，下线时也打声招呼（发现）。没有谁维护名单，可大家怎么知道该往哪儿喊、该在哪儿听？答案是一个人人都能算的公式。ROS 2 has no master. Each ROS 2 process is a "participant" in DDS; as soon as it starts, it multicasts "here I am" onto the local network, the other participants hear it and reply, and then the two sides exchange their endpoints: which topic I write, of what type, with what QoS; which topic I read … If the topic names and types match and the QoS is compatible, the pair is connected, and from then on the data goes peer to peer over UDP (on the same computer it can go through shared memory). Participants call out again at intervals, and say goodbye when they go offline (discovery). Nobody keeps a list, so how does everyone know where to call out and where to listen? The answer is a formula that anyone can work out.
    

    

    Pmc = 7400 + 250 · dPuc = 7400 + 250 · d + 10 + 2 · i
    

    

    域号为 d 的所有参与者，都在端口 7400 + 250 · d 上组播"我在这儿"；同一台电脑上的第 i 个参与者，在 7400 + 250 · d + 10 + 2 · i 上收专门发给它的发现消息（下一个端口收数据）。All participants with domain ID d multicast "here I am" on port 7400 + 250 · d; participant i on a computer receives the discovery messages meant for it alone on 7400 + 250 · d + 10 + 2 · i (and its data on the next port).
    

    没有电话簿，就得事先约好一个"集合地点"，而且这个地点只能从大家都知道的东西算出来。DDS 的线上协议 RTPS 规定了这套算法：先按域号把端口分成每 250 个一段，不同的域互不干扰；同一台电脑上的几个进程，再按序号各占两个端口，彼此不撞。ROS 用的"域号"就是环境变量 ROS_DOMAIN_ID，默认是 0。Fast DDS（默认的中间件）就照这个办法给每个进程分单播端口；Cyclone DDS 默认只有组播端口照公式，单播端口交给系统随便分。Without a phone book, everyone has to agree on a "meeting point" in advance, and that point can only be worked out from things everyone knows. RTPS, the DDS wire protocol, lays down the scheme: first the ports are split by domain ID into blocks of 250, so different domains do not interfere with each other; then the processes on one computer each take two ports according to their number, so they never collide. The "domain ID" that ROS uses is the environment variable ROS_DOMAIN_ID, 0 by default. Fast DDS (the default middleware) assigns each process its unicast ports in exactly this way; by default, Cyclone DDS follows the formula only for the multicast port and leaves the unicast ports for the system to assign as it pleases.
    

    

    d
    域号，ROS_DOMAIN_ID，默认 0；域号不同的节点互相看不见the domain ID, ROS_DOMAIN_ID, 0 by default; nodes with different domain IDs cannot see each other
    

    i
    这台电脑上同一个域里的第几个参与者（从 0 数起）；一个 ROS 2 进程一个参与者which participant this is in the same domain on this computer (counting from 0); one participant per ROS 2 process
    

    Pmc
    组播用的端口（发给所有人）the port used for multicast (sent to everyone)
    

    Puc
    单播用的端口（只发给这一个参与者的消息从这里收）the port used for unicast (messages meant only for this participant are received here)
    

    

    这些数和官方文档一致：域 0 的组播端口是 7400；域 1 是 7650，这台电脑上域 1 的第 0 个进程用 7660 和 7661，第 119 个进程用 7898 和 7899；第 120 个进程算出来是 7900 和 7901，正好撞上域 2 的组播端口。所以用 Fast DDS 时，一台电脑上同一个域里大约跑到 120 个进程就开始挤了。Linux 默认把 32768–60999 留给临时端口，按公式算，域号选 0 到 101（或 215 到 232）才不会撞上；不过域 101 最多只能跑 54 个进程，域 232 最多 63 个（域号）。The numbers match the official docs: domain 0’s multicast port is 7400; domain 1’s is 7650; on this computer, process 0 in domain 1 uses 7660 and 7661, and process 119 uses 7898 and 7899; process 120 works out to 7900 and 7901, which is exactly domain 2’s multicast port. So with Fast DDS, one domain on one computer starts to get crowded at about 120 processes. By default Linux keeps 32768–60999 for ephemeral ports, and by the formula only domain IDs 0 to 101 (or 215 to 232) stay clear of them; even then, domain 101 can run at most 54 processes and domain 232 at most 63 (domain IDs).
    

    "不要主节点"并不是免费的：每个参与者都要和每个参与者打招呼，进程一多，发现的消息就按进程数的平方涨；组播在 Wi-Fi 上又慢又容易丢，很多网络干脆不放行组播。所以后来有了几种补丁：Fast DDS 的发现服务器、只在本机发现的选项，以及 Zenoh。rmw_zenoh 默认关掉组播发现：每台电脑上跑一个路由程序 rmw_zenohd，节点先连上它，由它转告"谁在哪儿"，同一台电脑上的节点随后直接互连；要跨电脑，就把两台电脑上的路由程序连起来（rmw_zenoh）。绕了一圈，又回到了"有一个介绍人"，只是这回每台电脑一个，可以连成一张网；而且节点默认只在本机的回环地址上收连接，跨电脑的数据也要经两边的路由程序转一道。"No master" does not come free: every participant has to greet every other participant, so as the number of processes grows, the discovery messages grow with the square of that number; and multicast is slow and easily lost on Wi-Fi, and many networks simply block it. So several patches came later: Fast DDS’s discovery server, an option to discover only on the local machine, and Zenoh. rmw_zenoh turns multicast discovery off by default: each computer runs a router program, rmw_zenohd; nodes connect to it first, it tells them "who is where", and nodes on the same computer then connect to each other directly; to go across computers, you connect the routers on the two computers (rmw_zenoh). So things have come full circle, back to "having a go-between", only this time there is one on each computer, and they can be linked into a network; what is more, by default nodes accept connections only on the local loopback address, so data between computers also has to be relayed through the routers on both sides.
    

    

    服务质量：每个话题自己定规矩Quality of service: each topic sets its own rules
    

    ROS 1 里，同一个话题、同一种类型的发布者和订阅者一定会连上，传法基本只有 TCP（roscpp 另有一种很少用的 UDPROS）。ROS 2 让每个发布者和订阅者自己选服务质量（QoS）（QoS 文档）：In ROS 1, a publisher and a subscriber on the same topic with the same type always connect, and the transport is essentially only TCP (roscpp also has UDPROS, which is rarely used). ROS 2 lets each publisher and subscriber choose its own quality of service (QoS) (QoS docs):
    

      

    • 可靠性：可靠（丢了要重发）或尽力而为（丢了就算了）。注意在 DDS 里，"可靠"也是在 UDP 上实现的：发送方隔一会儿发一个"心跳"，说自己发到了第几号；接收方回报缺了哪几号，发送方再补（rmw_zenoh 则默认全走 TCP）。Reliability: reliable (anything lost is sent again) or best effort (anything lost is simply gone). Note that in DDS, "reliable" is also built on UDP: every so often the sender sends a "heartbeat" saying which number it has sent up to; the receiver reports which numbers are missing, and the sender fills the gaps (rmw_zenoh, by contrast, sends everything over TCP by default).
      • 

    • 历史和深度：队列里留最近的几条（比如 10 条），还是全留。History and depth: keep the last few messages in the queue (10, say), or keep them all.
      • 

    • 持久性：易失（只给订阅以后的新消息）或本地暂存（新来的订阅者能补到最近的几条，相当于 ROS 1 的"锁存"）。Durability: volatile (only new messages, from the moment of subscribing) or transient local (a subscriber that joins later can still get the last few, like "latching" in ROS 1).
      • 

    • 还有截止时间和活跃度，用来发现"该来的消息没来""发布者还在不在"；寿命则规定一条消息多久以后算过期，过期的直接丢掉，不交给订阅者。There are also deadline and liveliness, for spotting "a message that should have arrived has not" and "is the publisher still there?"; lifespan sets how long before a message counts as expired, and expired messages are dropped straight away rather than handed to the subscriber.
      • 

    

    默认的 QoS 是：留最近 10 条、可靠、易失。传感器数据另有一套预设：尽力而为、队列更短，因为一帧旧图重发过来已经没用了，还会挡住新图。两边的 QoS 不一定要相同，但要兼容：订阅者"要求"的不能比发布者"提供"的更严（这是 DDS 的规矩；rmw_zenoh 里几乎没有"不兼容"的 QoS，任何发布者都能配上任何订阅者）。The default QoS is: keep the last 10, reliable, volatile. Sensor data has a preset of its own: best effort, with a shorter queue, because an old image sent again is no use by the time it arrives, and it would hold up the new ones. The QoS on the two sides need not be the same, but it must be compatible: what the subscriber "requests" must not be stricter than what the publisher "offers" (this is the DDS rule; in rmw_zenoh there is almost no such thing as "incompatible" QoS, and any publisher can match any subscriber).
    

    

    发布者提供Publisher offers订阅者要求Subscriber requests连得上吗Connects?
    


    尽力而为Best effort尽力而为Best effort能Yes
    

    尽力而为Best effort可靠Reliable不能No
    

    可靠Reliable尽力而为Best effort能Yes
    

    可靠Reliable可靠Reliable能Yes
    

    易失Volatile本地暂存Transient local不能No
    

    本地暂存Transient local易失或本地暂存Volatile or transient local能Yes
    

    

    连不上时，两边各收到一个"QoS 不兼容"的事件，可数据一条也不会来。新手最常见的坑就在第二行：相机驱动用传感器预设（尽力而为）发图，自己写的订阅者用默认 QoS（可靠），话题列表里看得见，就是收不到。When they cannot connect, each side receives an "incompatible QoS" event, but not a single message gets through. The most common beginner’s trap is in the second row: the camera driver publishes images with the sensor-data preset (best effort), the subscriber you wrote yourself uses the default QoS (reliable), and the topic is there in the topic list, yet nothing arrives.
    

    类型、拷贝和代价Types, copies and costs
    

    消息类型仍然写在 .msg 文件里，比如 sensor_msgs/msg/Image：一个头（时间戳、坐标系名）、高、宽、编码、字节序、每行字节数、一个装像素的字节数组。编译时，rosidl 从它生成 C、C++、Python 的代码。从 Iron 起，每个类型在编译时还会算一个类型哈希（RIHS01），对方不认识的类型，可以通过一个服务把完整定义要过来（Iron 说明）。Message types are still written in .msg files, such as sensor_msgs/msg/Image: a header (time stamp, frame name), height, width, encoding, byte order, bytes per row, and a byte array holding the pixels. At build time, rosidl generates C, C++ and Python code from it. Since Iron, each type also gets a type hash (RIHS01) computed at build time, and when the other side does not know a type, it can ask for the full definition through a service (Iron release notes).
    

    同一台电脑上，默认的 Fast DDS 走共享内存传输，但仍然要序列化、拷进拷出。真正的"零拷贝"要发送方先向中间件借一块内存、直接把数据写进去（借出消息），而这要求中间件支持（官方文档里 rmw_fastrtps 支持，Cyclone DDS 和 Connext 不支持；用 Fast DDS 还得用 XML 另外打开它的 Data Sharing，默认是关的），而且类型必须是定长的"平"数据。图像消息里的像素数组是变长的，借不了（零拷贝文档）。所以大图像要省拷贝，常用的办法是下一步的"进程内通信"，或者 NVIDIA 的 NITROS 那样让数据一直留在 GPU 上（第 ⑬ 步）。On one computer, the default Fast DDS uses a shared-memory transport, but it still serialises and copies the data in and out. True "zero copy" needs the sender to first borrow a block of memory from the middleware and write the data straight into it (a loaned message), and that needs support from the middleware (according to the official docs, rmw_fastrtps supports it and Cyclone DDS and Connext do not; with Fast DDS you also have to switch on its Data Sharing separately in XML, as it is off by default); the type must also be fixed-size, "flat" data. The pixel array in an image message has a variable length, so it cannot be borrowed (zero-copy docs). So to save copies with large images, the usual approaches are the next step’s "intra-process communication", or keeping the data on the GPU all the way, as NVIDIA’s NITROS does (step ⑬).
    

    这几层也有代价。2021 年的一项测量发现，对小消息，ROS 2 比直接用 DDS 多花最多 50% 的延迟；消息从 128 字节到 10 KB，延迟几乎不变，到 100–500 KB 明显上升，因为 UDP 一个包最多 64 KB，大消息要拆成很多片；"可靠"比"尽力而为"最多多 15%（Kronauer 等）。另外有两件事 ROS 2 明说不保证：不同发行版的节点之间能正确通信，以及同一个发行版里不同中间件实现之间能互通（发行版列表）。These layers have a cost too. A 2021 measurement found that for small messages, ROS 2 adds up to 50% more latency than using DDS directly; from 128 bytes to 10 KB the latency hardly changes, but at 100–500 KB it rises clearly, because a UDP packet holds at most 64 KB and a large message has to be split into many fragments; "reliable" costs at most 15% more than "best effort" (Kronauer et al.). There are also two things ROS 2 says plainly that it does not guarantee: that nodes from different distributions communicate correctly, and that different middleware implementations in the same distribution can talk to each other (list of distributions).
    

      

    • 两个标签页。发现：三台机器 Thor、实时控制电脑和 Wi-Fi 那头的工作站，每个方框是一个参与者，里面是它的读写端点。▶ 播放、上一步、下一步、重来 依次走：在 239.255.0.1:7400 上组播"我在这儿"→ 交换端点信息（话题、类型、类型哈希、QoS）→ 匹配 → 点对点传数据 → 工作站上的 rviz2 晚加入。读数是参与者（进程）有几个、匹配上了几对、主节点（没有），以及发现时要传的信息量（示意）。Two tabs. Switch to "QoS", set the publisher to "Sensor data" and leave the subscriber on "Default": do they connect?
